title: Micro/Nanostructured Materials and Microfluidic Diagnostic Platforms Enable Multimodal Detection of Circulating Tumor Cells.
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs), as pivotal targets in liquid biopsy, offer dynamic, multidimensional insights into tumor heterogeneity and metastatic progression. However, their extreme rarity, pronounced heterogeneity, and the complexity of the blood microenvironment severely constrain detection accuracy. Advances in micro/nanomaterials and functional device engineering have enabled substantial improvements in CTC enrichment efficiency by refining the topographical and chemical properties of capture interfaces. These innovations also provide a compatible foundation for multimodal molecular profiling. This review systematically outlines the structure-function relationships of functionalized nanomaterials, microfiltration substrates, and biomimetic microfluidic devices, highlighting how material parameters-such as nanoscale architectures and membrane pore sizes-govern CTC capture performance. We further explore the integration of micro/nanomaterials with functional platforms for multidimensional molecular analyses across DNA, RNA, and protein levels. Coupled with emerging digital PCR technologies, these systems show promise in overcoming the sensitivity barriers associated with rare mutation detection and protein quantification, enabling multi-omics data fusion. We also discuss how artificial intelligence (AI)-driven feature selection, clustering, and prediction integrate multidimensional data to decode tumor heterogeneity and guide disease monitoring. Despite rapid progress, key challenges remain-including the lack of standardization, limited integration of multi-omic datasets, and the need for robust clinical validation. Future directions may lie in the convergence of microfluidic-integrated materials, single-cell multi-omics, and AI-driven analytics to establish dynamic, high-resolution monitoring platforms that bridge the gap between fundamental research and clinical precision oncology.

title: Network Biology: Current Status, Applications, Challenges, and Future Prospects.
abstract: Network biology provides a systems-level framework for understanding how interactions among molecular components, cells, microbial communities, tissues, and organs generate biological function and disease phenotypes. Recent advances in multiomics, single-cell and spatial profiling, network inference, organoid and organ-on-chip technologies, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence have shifted the field from static molecular maps toward dynamic, multiscale, and predictive network models. Major branches include molecular interaction networks, intracellular regulatory networks, single-cell and multicellular networks, microbial networks, disease networks, and interorgan interaction networks. Experimental and computational approaches are compared with respect to network reconstruction, causal validation, and cross-scale integration. Biomedical applications span disease classification, biomarker discovery, therapeutic-target identification, drug-response prediction, regenerative medicine, and precision healthcare. Particular emphasis is placed on interorgan interaction networks, in which carrier, route, range, timescale, recipient specificity, directionality, and feedback are treated as distinct mechanistic dimensions while mechanistic confidence is distinguished from translational maturity. Persistent challenges include incomplete context-specific network reconstruction, uncertain causal directionality, limited cross-scale integration, model interpretability, and insufficient clinical validation. Further progress will depend on integrating longitudinal and perturbation-resolved measurements with human-relevant experimental systems and multiscale computational models that quantify uncertainty and support prospective validation of patient-specific predictions.

title: Deep learning-based multiomics integration identifies AI-defined tissue regions associated with cancer-associated fibroblast enrichment and chemoresistance in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
abstract: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) frequently develops resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy, and tools for characterizing treatment-associated tumor microenvironmental features remain limited. We developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework integrating pathological imaging, multiomics data, single-cell RNA sequencing, and ex vivo drug-sensitivity testing. Three convolutional neural network models trained using hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained whole-slide images from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) classified tumor, necrosis, and lymphocyte-enriched regions and were evaluated in an independent tissue microarray cohort. Patches negative for all three classifiers were designated AI-defined "Other" regions; this residual category was not trained as a cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) classifier. Higher Other% was associated with shorter overall survival in univariable analyses, but the association was not significant after multivariable adjustment in TCGA. Multiomics and tissue-origin analyses linked Other% to stromal content. Scissor analysis of eight single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets identified Other-associated Scissor+ cells across epithelial and fibroblast compartments, while ACTA2 expression and extracellular matrix-remodeling pathways were enriched. In 48 MIBC specimens assessed by the hydrogel-embedded histoculture drug sensitivity test, Other% was higher in the gemcitabine-cisplatin-resistant group. Multiplex immunofluorescence further showed enrichment of alpha-smooth muscle actin signal in AI-defined Other regions. Erdafitinib showed ex vivo activity in a subset of specimens, but FGFR alteration status was unavailable and clinical efficacy was not evaluated. These findings support an association between AI-defined Other regions, CAF-related stromal features, and chemoresistance, while prospective validation is required before clinical use.

title: Single-cell Transcriptomics in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanistic Insights, Cross-disease Convergence, and Translational Challenges in Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Type 1 Diabetes, and Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Autoimmune diseases are characterized by loss of immune tolerance and substantial heterogeneity across patients, tissues, and disease stages. Although bulk transcriptomic studies have identified important inflammatory pathways, they cannot directly resolve rare, transitional, and tissue-contextualized cell states that may be relevant to disease mechanisms and therapeutic response. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables transcriptomic profiling at cellular resolution, while complementary multimodal, receptor-repertoire, epigenomic, and spatial approaches can link cellular states to protein phenotype, clonal architecture, regulatory programs, and tissue context. This review critically examines recent single-cell studies in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis, type 1 diabetes, and multiple sclerosis. Rather than providing a descriptive catalogue of published studies, we assess the strength of available evidence by distinguishing independently replicated findings from observations supported by limited studies, and cross-sectional associations from longitudinal, treatment-response, and functional evidence. Across the selected diseases, studies repeatedly report inflammatory programs involving interferon signaling, chemokine-mediated immune recruitment, and stromal-immune interactions; however, evidence for convergence at the cell-state and regulatory-network levels remains limited, and the extent to which shared signatures represent common pathogenic mechanisms rather than inflammatory context remains uncertain. We evaluate the translational potential of scRNA-seq for biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and treatment response prediction, while considering evidence from related tissue-based molecular stratification approaches, including the R4RA randomized trial in rheumatoid arthritis. R4RA provides prospective randomized evidence that synovial molecular features can enrich for differential therapeutic responses, but its use of bulk synovial transcriptomics and histopathology does not constitute prospective validation of single-cell-derived biomarkers. We further highlight cohort biases, reproducibility challenges, dissociation artifacts, computational ambiguity, and privacy concerns that constrain immediate clinical implementation. Together, these advances position single-cell profiling as a mechanistic discovery platform with substantial translational promise, contingent on standardization, validation across diverse cohorts, and integration with functional perturbation approaches.

title: Testing the Transferability of Perturbational Similarity Maps Across Species, Cell Systems, and Assay Modalities.
abstract: We evaluated a mouse whole-brain perturbation map in human K562 and RPE1 Perturb-seq, HeLa morphology and nine L1000 cell-line matrices using three endpoints: global pair-rank concordance, source-defined top-k neighbour preservation, and within-validation CORUM retrieval. Strict orthology retained 71, 90, 695 and 273-311 shared targets, respectively. Under the primary zero-anchored RMS representation, Spearman rho was 0.026 and 0.035 in K562 and RPE1, 0.0022 and 0.0055 in the two HeLa conditions, and a median of 0.0055 across L1000 lines. RPE1 depended on representation: across-target standardisation gave rho = 0.102 (95% CI, 0.027-0.201), whereas omitting feature RMS scaling gave a descriptive rho = -0.034. No source-defined top-10 neighbour preservation result survived correction across 13 contexts (minimum q = 0.240). Source pair ranks also changed when response features were restricted. Within-validation CORUM retrieval identified complex structure in several external matrices but did not test preservation of source neighbours. Across 50 cell splits, K562/RPE1 median global rho was 0.600/0.710 and top-10 overlap was 0.497/0.517. Across 50 mouse-level splits of K562/RPE1-matched source profiles, median global rho was 0.731/0.703; a cross-species noise ceiling remains unestimated. The results are conditional on representation and feature selection and do not establish absence of transfer or transferability to neural systems.

llm.summary_zh: 研究以小鼠全脑扰动图谱为基础，在人类K562与RPE1 Perturb-seq、HeLa形态学及多个L1000细胞系中检验迁移性，采用全局秩相关与近邻保留等指标。结果显示跨物种、跨模态的相关性很弱，多数上下文的近邻保留不显著。

title: Interpretable multi-omics learning with cell-conditioned motif graphs for drug response prediction
abstract: Cancer drug response prediction (DRP) remains a challenging problem due to the intrinsic heterogeneity of tumors and the dependence of structure-activity relationships on cellular context. Most existing approaches rely on single-omics data and global molecular representations, limiting their ability to capture how specific chemical substructures, known as motifs, interact with complex cellular states. We present C ell- C onditioned M otif G raph (CCMG), a graph-based framework that explicitly models interactions between molecular motifs and multi-omics cellular context for accurate and interpretable DRP. CCMG augments molecular graphs with motif-level representations and integrates them with cell-specific multi-omics embeddings through a unified graph structure, enabling context-aware learning of structure-activity relationships. This design allows the model to capture fine-grained substructure-cell interactions while enabling interpretability at the atom, motif, and gene levels. We evaluate CCMG on the Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer (GDSC) under several data-splitting schemes and conduct ablations to quantify each component’s contribution. Results demonstrate that explicit motif-cell coupling improves generalization over late-fusion baselines, particularly under challenging splits, while offering mechanistic insights that support downstream biological interpretation and clinical hypothesis generation.

title: Mapping transcriptional responses to cellular perturbations with RNA fingerprinting.
abstract: Single-cell perturbation dictionaries measure how cells respond to genetic and chemical perturbations, creating the opportunity to assign causal interpretations to observational data. We introduce RNA fingerprinting, a statistical framework that maps transcriptional responses from new experiments onto reference perturbation dictionaries. RNA fingerprinting learns perturbation representations, or "fingerprints," from single-cell data, then probabilistically assigns query cells to one or more candidate perturbations. We benchmark on ground-truth datasets, demonstrating accurate assignments at single-cell resolution, scalability to genome-wide screens, and the ability to resolve combinatorial perturbations. We demonstrate broad utility across diverse biological settings: identifying context-specific regulators of p53 under ribosomal stress, characterizing dose-dependent drug mechanisms of action, and uncovering cytokine-driven B cell heterogeneity during secondary influenza infection in vivo. Together, these results establish RNA fingerprinting as a versatile framework for interpreting single-cell datasets by linking cellular states to their underlying perturbations.

title: Multimodal spatial transcriptomics redefines cortical pathology in Huntington’s disease
abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is caused by CAG expansion in the huntingtin gene (HTT), yet how somatic repeat instability and HTT inclusions relate to selective cell loss in the human brain remains unclear. We have developed a multimodal spatial transcriptomics approach that enables the definition of transcriptional programs with subcellular resolution, somatic CAG repeat lengths, and eight other pathology markers, including HTT inclusions, in every cell of intact brain sections. Imaging 428,173 cells in the control and HD cortex revealed the selective vulnerability of layer 5-6 (L5-6) near-projecting (NP) neurons and L6b deep-layer excitatory neurons, which undergo a >50% loss that is closely linked to large somatic repeat expansions (>450 ± 55 CAGs). Intranuclear inclusions were most prevalent at intermediate somatic repeat expansions (250-350 CAGs) and were associated with broader transcriptional changes than somatic repeat expansion alone. These data provide a comprehensive resource and establish a general framework for connecting repeat expansion and protein pathology across diverse cell types.

title: Quantifying the impact of genetic mutations on enhancer dynamics
abstract: Transcriptional regulation is mediated by enhancers, yet how genetic perturbations alter enhancer activity and gene expression remains unclear. We develop UDI-UMI-STARR-seq, integrating dual indexes and unique molecular identifiers, and combine it with RNA-seq to profile perturbation-associated changes in enhancer activity and gene expression. We apply this approach to 253,632 fragments representing 46,142 cell type-specific candidate enhancers and assess the impact of CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of six transcription factors (ATF2, CTCF, FOXA1, LEF1, TCF7L2, and SCRT1). We identify responsive fragments that are repressed or induced and enriched for p53 family motifs. Enhancer-gene mapping reveals associations between responsive fragments and gene expression changes, including Wnt/p53 targets after ATF2 or LEF1 depletion. A deep learning model recapitulates enhancer grammar, including cooperative motif syntax and flanking sequence context. Applying this framework to 16p12.1 deletion identifies responsive fragments associated with genes involved in neuronal function, providing a scalable readout of enhancer dynamics across genetic perturbations.

title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals archetypal regulatory programs shared across T cell subsets
abstract: T cells differentiate into functionally distinct subsets in response to pathogens, yet essential immune functions such as self-renewal, expansion, cytokine production, and cytotoxicity are common to multiple subsets and therefore must be programmed via shared regulatory mechanisms. To uncover these "archetypal" epigenomic programs, we integrated a single-cell multiomic (scATAC+RNA-seq) dataset of CD4 and CD8 T cells responding to acute and chronic viral infection with a comprehensive bulk ATAC-seq compendium. Our analysis reveals a modular architecture governing T cell identity, implicating distinct transcription factors in reusing regulatory programs across subsets and lineages. Notably, translationally important progenitor CD8 T cells, critical for sustained immunity and present in both acute and chronic infection, exhibit a composite regulatory state, combining a CD8 exhaustion program with a follicular helper CD4 T cell program. In sum, this resource and generalizable computational framework will aid the mechanistic dissection of adaptive immunity and immunotherapy design.

llm.novelty_zh: 整合单细胞scATAC+RNA数据与bulk ATAC-seq汇编，识别跨CD4与CD8 T细胞亚群共享的表观调控程序。
llm.summary_zh: 研究将CD4和CD8 T细胞在急性与慢性病毒感染下的单细胞多组学数据与bulk ATAC-seq汇编整合，识别调控模块与转录因子。作者发现前体CD8 T细胞同时具有衰竭程序与滤泡辅助CD4 T细胞程序的复合调控状态。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该结果为理解适应性免疫中的共享调控逻辑及免疫治疗设计提供了资源与框架。

title: Sequential TPRX1 and HERVL activation delineates a progression toward the totipotent-like state
abstract: The in vitro induction of 8-cell-like cells (8CLCs) from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) provides a model to study the regulatory principles of totipotency and zygotic genome activation (ZGA). However, the cellular dynamics underlying 8CLC emergence remain poorly understood. Here, we generate a TPRX1-EGFP/HERVL-tdTomato dual-reporter hPSC line to resolve the stepwise acquisition of totipotent-like identity. We show that 8CLC induction follows an ordered trajectory in which TPRX1 activation precedes the emergence of TPRX1+HERVL+ cells, which most closely resemble the in vivo 8-cell embryo transcriptionally. Single-cell transcriptomics and time-resolved flow cytometry further define a continuous transition from the primed state through a TPRX1+ intermediate to the HERVL+ 8CLC state. CRISPRi and RNA-directed perturbations support functional contributions of HERVL elements and HERVL-derived RNA to this transition, while potential locus-dependent mechanisms remain unresolved. Together, these findings establish sequential TPRX1 and HERVL activation as a defining feature of human 8CLC induction.

title: Deep Lineage: Single-cell lineage tracing and fate inference using deep learning
abstract: Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing and lineage tracing techniques have provided valuable insights into the temporal changes in gene expression during development, tumor progression, and disease onset. However, there are few computational methods available to analyze this information to help understand multicellular dynamics. We introduce Deep Lineage, a deep-learning method for analyzing time-series single-cell RNA sequencing with matched lineage tracing data. Our method accurately predicts early cell fate biases and gene expression profiles at different time points within a clone, surpassing existing methods in fate prediction accuracy. We further validate our model using LineageSim, a fate-aware lineage simulator, demonstrating robustness to technical noise such as barcode dropout and clone misidentification. Additionally, we apply Deep Lineage to in silico perturbations in cellular reprogramming and hematopoiesis to identify key genes and pathways associated with cell fate determination and propose testable perturbation hypotheses for experimental follow-up.

title: Cervical cancer survival analysis by integrating multi-omics data through an adaptive weighted deep neural network.
abstract: Accurately analyzing cervical cancer prognosis holds significant importance for enhancing clinical outcomes within the framework of precision medicine. Since single-omics data only capture a limited perspective of cervical cancer patients, integrating multiple types of omics data is essential to provide more comprehensive insights. However, capturing the key information in multi-omics data fusion remains challenging owing to the presence of a large number of redundant variables and a relatively small sample size. In this study, we propose a deep neural network called AWMP to better integrate multi-omics data for cervical cancer survival analysis. The experiment demonstrated that AWMP enhances cancer prognosis prediction by 4.74% relative to the mean performance of the four comparator methods, benefiting from its adaptive weighted mechanism that effectively addresses the greedy nature of learning in multi-omics integration. In this study, based on the risk subgroups stratified by AWMP, four key genes (CDC42BPB, KLRG1, MAP7, LIMD2) are identified as been highly associated with cervical cancer prognosis and immune cell infiltration, highlighting their role in tumor heterogeneity. Additionally, single-cell tumor heterogeneity analysis revealed that the B-cell C2 subset correlates with both prognosis and immune response in cervical cancer, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic target. These findings underscore the accuracy and biological relevance of our deep learning framework for multi-omics integration in cervical cancer prognosis. Collectively, the identification of B-cell C2 subset advances the understanding of the precise role of B cells in cancer immune evasion and paves the way for more effective immunotherapy for cervical cancer.

title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

title: InDyVAE: An interaction and dependency-aware variational autoencoder for single-cell perturbation response generation.
abstract: Single-cell perturbation profiling provides a powerful means of studying how genetic interventions reshape cellular transcription, but only a small portion of the possible perturbation space can be measured experimentally. Predicting the remaining conditions requires more than transferring an average treatment effect: jointly applied perturbations may alter one another, cellular and technical states modulate the observed response, and the resulting latent variation must be faithfully expressed at the gene level. We address these coupled requirements with InDyVAE, an interaction- and dependency-aware variational autoencoder that models response generation as a connected sequence of transformations. Perturbation Interaction Learning (PIL) represents the effects of active interventions in a shared context, allowing each treatment's contribution to reflect its co-occurring perturbations while preserving its individual signal. Latent State Dependency Modeling (LSDM) then conditions the perturbation response on basal cellular and quality-associated states, retaining the distinct roles of these sources of variation. Nonlinear Expression Mapping (NEM) translates the integrated state into gene expression through a direct pathway complemented by localized functional responses in latent space. We evaluate InDyVAE on four Perturb-seq datasets using treatment-effect agreement, top-gene overlap, and quality-control compliance under three thresholds. Comparisons with recent reference models, including CRADLE-VAE and AttentionPert, show strong response recovery on Norman and metric-dependent trade-offs between response accuracy and rule-based QC pass rates on Dixit. For single-gene interventions, it achieves higher quality-control pass rates on Replogle and stronger treatment-effect estimates on Adamson, while the remaining comparisons are dataset- and metric-dependent. Ablation experiments further show that the three components contribute complementary capabilities, supporting the proposed organization of interaction, context, and expression modeling. Source code is available at https://github.com/yuqi0373-rgb/InDyVAE.

title: Standardizing spatial transcriptomic analysis for infectious diseases with STID
abstract: Spatial transcriptomic studies of infectious diseases still rely on fragmented data analysis processes. Here, we developed STID (spatial transcriptomics toolkit for infectious diseases), a standardized framework for spatial transcriptomic analysis of infectious diseases that leverages the Seurat ecosystem and incorporates Python-based modules. STID provides an extensible infection-specific data structure and supports a full suite of analyses, such as pathogen background correction, infection-associated spot and niche identification, single-sample niche characterization, and multi-sample comparative and temporal analyses. STID is broadly applicable to spatial transcriptomic data from infectious diseases caused by bacteria, viruses, and parasites and enables systematic characterization of the structural features, cellular composition, molecular functions, and host-pathogen interactions within pathogen-infected and/or host-responsive niches. Overall, STID provides an accessible, reproducible, and extensible framework for analyzing infection-associated spatial transcriptomic data and for dissecting host-pathogen interactions in their native spatial microenvironments.

title: Geometric inference of cross-species transcriptome correspondence
abstract: Sequence homology reveals evolutionary gene correspondences, but identifying functionally corresponding genes within specific cell types or during cell fate specification remains non-trivial. Here, frameworks that translate insights from model organisms into other species would accelerate wet-lab studies, so we develop Species-OT, a cross-species transcriptome analysis framework using Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport, which quantitatively compares the geometry of transcriptome distributions. Given a pair of bulk or single-cell RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets, Species-OT returns a gene-to-gene correspondence capturing probabilistic alignments of regulatory roles and a transcriptomic distance quantifying overall divergence. Applied pairwise, Species-OT yields a transcriptomic discrepancy array and a hierarchical clustering tree analogous to a phylogenetic tree. We validate Species-OT using bulk RNA-seq data for cell fate specification from pluripotent stem cells in mice, monkeys, and humans and single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data from pluripotent stem cells of six mammalian species. Species-OT identifies gene correspondences within cell fate specification, while transcriptomic discrepancies recapitulate expected species relationships.

title: Emerging frontiers for AI in single-cell genomics.
abstract: We are just over a decade into the single-cell revolution in biology, which has been coupled to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in single-cell genomics. Most early single-cell RNA embedding models and subsequent "foundation models"-representational models pretrained on large single-cell datasets-did not gain wide traction among experimental biologists. However, as massive single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas efforts ramp up, there is a clear rationale for exploiting AI models to interpret new datasets in the context of vast existing data resources. Meanwhile, the advent of single-cell epigenetic/multiomic assays and Perturb-seq technologies presents new opportunities for AI modeling. Here, we review AI embedding and foundation models for scRNA-seq and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), extensive machine-learning efforts to exploit single-cell multiome in regulatory genomics, and AI strategies to learn "virtual cell" models from Perturb-seq, ending with a description of current limitations of single-cell AI models and an outlook for future advances.

title: From holism to single-cell resolution: Applications and advances of scRNA-seq in pharmacological research of TCM and compound formulas
abstract: Background Conventional approaches struggle to dissect the “multi-component, multi-target, multi-pathway” mode of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). Bulk RNA sequencing averages signals across cells, masking heterogeneity and differential drug responses. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables systematic resolution of these complex effects at single-cell resolution. Methods This study conducted a systematic literature search across PubMed, the Web of Science Core Collection, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), up to August 2026. Additionally, through reverse citation tracing of the included studies and relevant reviews, additional literature records were identified. All studies that met the predefined inclusion criteria were retrieved, critically assessed, and subjected to a comprehensive thematic analysis. Results scRNA-seq has enabled precise identification of cellular targets, revealed drug-induced immune microenvironment remodeling, and deconvoluted multi-pathway networks underlying TCM actions. Integrating spatial transcriptomics, multi-omics, and AI deepens mechanistic understanding. Key challenges include tissue dissociation bias, batch effects, spatial context loss, limited animal model translatability, and insufficient data standardization. Conclusion This review consolidates advances in single-cell transcriptomics for TCM research and outlines future directions including multimodal integration, organoid models, and clinical cohort studies. It provides a mechanistic reference to accelerate TCM modernization from holism into single-cell precision.

title: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.
abstract: Background Cancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance. Methods We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from 92,218 cells across 13 treatment-naïve BLCA samples to characterize epithelial stemness and tumor-microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics and independent bulk cohorts were used for orthogonal and clinical validation. An HStem-associated histopathology-based prognostic model was developed by integrating quantitative image features with deep-learning representations, followed by functional validation of the candidate gene C11orf24. Results We identified a highly stem-like epithelial population (HStem) at the apex of the differentiation hierarchy, exhibiting MYC activation, oxidative phosphorylation, and DNA repair enrichment, with preferential presence in advanced-stage tumors. HStem cells were inferred to serve as major communication hubs within the TME, interacting extensively with fibroblasts and endothelial cells via MIF-CD74/CXCR4 and MIF-CD74/CD44 axes. An 86-gene HStem signature enabled development of a robust image-based prognostic model. High-risk tumors showed immune exclusion, immunosuppressive enrichment, T-cell dysfunction, and predicted checkpoint blockade resistance. C11orf24 emerged as a candidate stemness-associated regulator; C11orf24-positive cells displayed enhanced stemness and stromal interactions. Functional experiments demonstrated that C11orf24 perturbation altered clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion in BLCA cells. Pharmacogenomic analyses identified predicted therapeutic vulnerabilities that warrant experimental validation. Conclusions We identify an HStem population associated with BLCA progression, microenvironmental remodeling, and immune evasion. Integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with computational pathology, we establish a clinically relevant stemness framework and identify C11orf24 as a potential therapeutic target, offering opportunities for stemness-directed precision oncology.

title: NF-κB–mediated chemoresistance emerges from distorted fallopian tube cell-state trajectory in ovarian cancer
abstract: Homeostatic gene expression programs persist through oncogenesis, creating new malignant states that adapt to therapies. To reveal how fallopian tube epithelia (FTE) cell states transform into intra-tumoral heterogeneity in ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), we analysed treatment-naive tumors (n = 50) and normal FTE (n = 14) by single cell transcriptomics, identifying tissue-specific transcriptional modules gained, lost, or conserved through carcinogenesis. Of these, two conserved, opposing modules associated with survival and showed genetic biases, suggesting that oncogenic drivers employ existing epithelial programs. Challenging the cancer stem cell paradigm, a developmentally early oxidative-phosphorylation module was associated with improved survival, whereas the developmentally late MAPK/NF-κB module defined a stable, chemoresistant state that had lost the MHC II antigen presentation of the corresponding normal FTE state. Using these modules to predict perturbations capable of shifting cell-state dynamics, we demonstrate in patient-derived organoid models that restraining ER stress via SERCA2 activation drives a resistant, NF-κB–active phenotype, whereas inhibiting the DNA repair regulator CCDC6 promotes the opposite, platinum-sensitive state. Our study suggests that conserved tissue-of-origin states, rather than de novo cancer states, drive the key cell state dynamic and clinical response heterogeneity of HGSC and can be targeted in vitro to modulate platinum response.

llm.novelty_zh: 利用单细胞模块预测可改变细胞状态动态的扰动，并在患者来源类器官中验证 SERCA2 激活与 CCDC6 抑制的相反效应。
llm.summary_zh: 作者分析了 50 例未治疗高级别浆液性卵巢癌与 14 例正常输卵管上皮的单细胞转录组，鉴定出与生存相关的保守模块，其中 MAPK/NF-κB 模块对应化疗耐药状态。研究基于这些模块预测扰动，并在患者来源类器官中证实 SERCA2 激活诱导耐药表型，CCDC6 抑制诱导铂敏感表型。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 将细胞状态动态与扰动预测结合并以类器官验证，为卵巢癌化疗耐药干预提供了线索。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Syndecan-3 couples tumor mechanics to immunosuppressive macrophage identity
abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages adopt suppressive states, but how tumor stress installs these programs remains unclear. Here, we identify syndecan-3 (SDC3) as a macrophage-intrinsic mechanosensory regulator by integrating in vivo functional screening, single-cell and spatial profiling, and genetic and pharmacological perturbation. SDC3 + macrophages accumulate in hypoxic, stiff tumor niches and suppress antitumor cytotoxic T-cell responses. Matrix stiffness increases mechanical loading on SDC3, reorganizes an SDC3-associated scaffold and opens suppressive chromatin loci. This program engages a CDK7–MAFB relay to induce TREM2, which functions as a required suppressive effector in mice. Human-cell assays support a species-specific TREM2-associated inhibition mechanism. Naldemedine engages TREM2, restores cytotoxic T-cell activity, improves tumor control and enhances immune-checkpoint blockade in vivo. These findings define a targetable SDC3–CDK7–MAFB–TREM2 axis linking hypoxia and tissue mechanics to macrophage-mediated immune evasion.
affiliations: The First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University
Hospital of Stomatology, Sun Yat-sen University

llm.novelty_zh: 发现基质硬度通过SDC3-CDK7-MAFB-TREM2轴驱动肿瘤巨噬细胞的免疫抑制状态。
llm.summary_zh: 研究鉴定了巨噬细胞内在的机械感受因子SDC3，其在缺氧和高硬度肿瘤微环境中富集并抑制细胞毒性T细胞。作者通过小鼠实验证明TREM2是必需的抑制效应分子，并显示萘地美坦可靶向TREM2增强免疫检查点阻断效果。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为肿瘤免疫逃逸的机械调控机制提供了潜在药物靶点。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要提到人源细胞实验显示的抑制机制具有物种特异性。

title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
abstract: The cellular complexity of adipose tissue plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease; however, mechanisms underlying adipose dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed a single-nucleus and bulk transcriptomic atlas of human visceral adipose tissues from an ethnically homogeneous cohort with defined metabolic states: lean with normal glucose tolerance, obesity, and obesity with type 2 diabetes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed a fibro-inflammatory subpopulation of adipose stem cells and adipocytes characterized by high THBS1 expression, which were enriched in individuals with obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes compared to lean controls. Through complementary in vitro (human primary ASCs, THP-1 macrophages, and Matrigel-captured mature adipocytes), ex vivo (mouse and human visceral adipose tissue explants), and in vivo (gain-of-function and antibody-mediated neutralization) experiments, we demonstrated that THBS1 promoted adipose fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage-mediated TGFβ activation, impairing adipogenesis and adipocyte function. Inhibition of THBS1 attenuated fibro-inflammatory features in metabolically dysfunctional adipose tissues. Moreover, THBS1 levels in plasma and adipocytes correlated with metabolic traits, including BMI and HbA1c. Collectively, our study provides a cellular atlas of human visceral adipose tissues across metabolic disease states and identifies THBS1 as a key pathogenic driver and potential therapeutic target.
affiliations: Pohang University of Science and Technology

llm.novelty_zh: 发现高表达 THBS1 的纤维炎症亚群，并证明其通过巨噬细胞 TGFβ 活化驱动脂肪纤维化。
llm.summary_zh: 研究构建了不同代谢状态人群的内脏脂肪单核与批量转录组图谱，识别出高表达 THBS1 的纤维炎症干细胞与脂肪细胞亚群。作者通过体外、离体及体内实验证明，THBS1 经巨噬细胞 TGFβ 活化促进脂肪纤维化与炎症，并与 BMI、HbA1c 等代谢指标相关。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该研究提出 THBS1 作为代谢性疾病的潜在治疗靶点，属于疾病机制与转化研究，与虚拟细胞建模没有直接关联。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
abstract: The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.
affiliations: Robert H. Lurie Comprehensive Cancer Center of Northwestern University

llm.novelty_zh: 阐明miR-200通过抑制SOX9及WNT相关负调控因子来阻断皮脂腺命运的分子机制。
llm.summary_zh: 研究发现miR-200在毛基质祖细胞中高表达，而在上部毛囊中缺失。异位诱导miR-200会阻断皮脂腺特化，同时保留毛发形态发生。通过靶标鉴定和SOX9靶标分析，研究揭示了一条空间有序的调控网络，其中包含脂质代谢程序。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 揭示了上皮发育中微小RNA调控细胞命运与增殖的空间机制。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals microenvironmental heterogeneity in osteoarthritic subchondral bone
abstract: Although increasing evidence implicates subchondral bone alterations in osteoarthritis, the spatial organization of subchondral bone remodeling remains unclear. Applying spatial transcriptomics to human subchondral bone, we identify a spatially conserved osteogenic core-halo architecture that displays transcriptional reprogramming in sclerotic microenvironments. Spatial dependency and a customized cell-cell communication framework reveal disrupted osteoblast-osteoclast spatial coupling, enhanced osteoblast-mesenchymal interactions, and identify FN1-SDC2 and COL1A1-DDR2 as candidate stromal-osteogenic signaling axes that may contribute to aberrant bone remodeling. Additionally, we present the in situ transcriptional landscape of osteocytes and reveal its potential regulatory role in aberrant bone remodeling. We further delineate a continuum of spatial ecotypes exhibiting distinct enrichment, spatial topology reorganization, and inter-ecotype communication rewiring across pathological states. Metabolic flux inference additionally reveals substrate-limited, stressed states across multiple ecotypes in sclerotic microenvironments. Collectively, our findings provide critical insights into aberrant subchondral bone remodeling in osteoarthritis and offer a valuable framework for future mechanistic studies and therapeutic exploration.

llm.novelty_zh: 在人软骨下骨中识别出成骨核心-晕空间结构，并提出 FN1-SDC2 与 COL1A1-DDR2 等候选信号轴。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究对人软骨下骨进行空间转录组分析，识别出保守的成骨核心-晕结构及其在硬化微环境中的转录重编程。作者还描绘了空间生态型的连续谱，并推断病理状态下的细胞通讯重布线与代谢受限状态，以解释异常骨重塑。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该研究为骨关节炎异常骨重塑的空间机制提供线索，属于疾病组织学分析，与虚拟细胞建模没有直接关系。

title: Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis
abstract: IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, we conduct genome, transcriptome, and proteome-wide association studies in 2170 IgA vasculitis cases and 5928 controls, generate IgA vasculitis-specific maps of gene expression and splicing from blood of 255 pediatric cases, and reconstruct myeloid-specific regulatory networks to define disease master regulators modulated by the identified genes. We observe significant association at the HLA-DRB1 locus (OR = 1.55, P = 1.1 × 10-25) and fine-map specific amino-acid risk substitutions in DRβ1. We find two novel non-HLA associated loci: FCAR (OR = 1.51, P = 1.0 × 10-20), encoding a myeloid IgA receptor FcαR, and INPP5D (OR = 1.34, P = 2.2 × 10-09), encoding an inhibitor of FcαR signalling. The FCAR risk locus co-localizes with a cis-eQTL that increases FCAR expression; the risk alleles disrupt a PRDM1 binding motif within a myeloid enhancer of FCAR. Another risk locus is associated with higher genetically predicted levels of plasma IL6R. The IL6R risk haplotype carries a missense variant contributing to accelerated cleavage of IL6R into a soluble form. Applying network-based approaches to blood single cell transcriptomes, we predict, independently replicate, and experimentally validate 21 IgA vasculitis master regulators co-modulated by FCAR, INPP5D and IL6R signalling in myeloid cells.

title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model
abstract: Dynamic remodeling of immune cell-surface glycans reflects cellular state and immune activity. Despite advances in single-cell glyco-profiling, current methods primarily capture pre-existing glycan epitopes, providing limited information on dynamic sialoglycans. Here, we present GlycoStamp-seq, a method to profile nascent sialoglycan dynamics by coupling Ac₄ManNAz-based metabolic glycoengineering with single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) and scDyna-seq. We apply GlycoStamp-seq by injecting Ac₄ManNAz into oxaliplatin-treated mice with subcutaneous bladder tumors, days before extracting tumor-derived single-cell suspensions for sequencing. Following oxaliplatin treatment, a subset of CD8⁺ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment exhibits elevated nascent sialoglycan activity, enhanced effector programs, and increased clonal expansion. Furthermore, elevated nascent sialoglycan levels mark antigen-reactive CD8⁺ T cells with increased anti-tumor efficacy in vitro and in vivo. GlycoStamp-seq may thus serve as a versatile platform for profiling nascent sialoglycan dynamics in complex tissues, thereby expanding the single-cell multi-omics toolkit and providing insights into sialoglycan dynamics during therapeutic response.
affiliations: Nanjing General Hospital of Nanjing Military Command

llm.novelty_zh: 将代谢糖工程的新生糖链标记与单细胞测序相结合，实现单细胞层面的糖组动态分析。
llm.summary_zh: GlycoStamp-seq利用Ac4ManNAz代谢标记结合scRNA/TCR测序，检测肿瘤免疫细胞中的新生唾液酸聚糖动态。在奥沙利铂处理的膀胱肿瘤小鼠中，高新生糖水平的CD8+ T细胞表现出更强的效应和抗肿瘤能力。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为研究治疗应答中免疫细胞糖组动态提供了单细胞多组学方法。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及该方法在其他模型中的适用性。

title: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning
abstract: Proteins are the main drivers of cell function and disease, making proteomics a powerful technique for biomarker discovery and defining cell identity. While current technologies can profile thousands of proteins and reach single-cell sensitivity, limited throughput restricts applications such as robust classification of large biological or clinical cohorts. To close this gap, we present a deep-learning (DL) approach for the direct analysis of mass spectrometric (MS) data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identity. Specifically, we introduce the ProFormer, a transformer pipeline that classifies samples by tabular MS1-level features derived from peptide ions, eliminating the need for time-consuming data interpretation. The ProFormer outperforms traditional machine-learning and image-based convolutional neural networks (CNNs), demonstrating enhanced classification and generalization over 14 evaluated architectures. We further provide detailed insights into how the ProFormer dynamically aggregates MS1 data, while preserving signal contribution and enabling explainable AI at single-peptide resolution. Applied to diverse LC-MS data sets, the ProFormer accurately classified single-cell proteomes by cell type, cycle stage or differentiation trajectory, as well as patient disease status from plasma proteomes. Thereby, the ProFormer provides a versatile and rapid framework for the classification of proteomic data, with important implications for patient stratification, early detection and single-cell analysis.

title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program.

llm.summary_zh: 该研究利用 Visium 空间转录组分析 COVID-19 与对照肺组织，报告内皮细胞、I 型肺泡细胞和自然杀伤细胞减少，而髓系细胞与基质细胞（主要为支气管周围成纤维细胞）增加，并指出 TGF-β 通路在弥漫性肺泡损伤中起驱动作用。作者还描绘了肺泡上皮再生的时空轨迹。

title: Interpretable and scalable spatial gene set activity analysis with GESSO uncovers functional tissue architecture
abstract: Spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) measures gene expression within tissues. Existing methods that summarize the activity of functionally related genes often ignore relationships between neighboring locations and offer limited statistical testing, gene-level interpretation, or scalability. Here we present GESSO, a method that incorporates spatial information to estimate gene set activity within tissues, quantify how strongly each gene contributes to the resulting activity scores, and perform location-specific statistical tests for elevated pathway activity. In simulations and analyses of 13 datasets from five SRT platforms, GESSO better recovers known spatial patterns, provides well-calibrated statistical tests and interpretable gene-level contributions, and scales more efficiently than existing methods. Applications across tumor, embryonic, and lymphoid tissues reveal localized biological programs, including epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition at tumor-stroma interfaces, developmental signaling gradients, and coordinated immune pathways within germinal centers. Therefore, GESSO enables interpretable and scalable spatial mapping of gene set activity across diverse SRT technologies and biological settings.

llm.novelty_zh: 将空间邻域信息纳入基因集活性估计，并提供位置特异的统计检验。
llm.summary_zh: GESSO 是一种空间转录组基因集活性估计方法，利用空间邻接信息计算活性分数，并量化各基因对分数的贡献。作者在模拟数据及五种平台的 13 个数据集上验证了其空间模式恢复、统计校准与可扩展性。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该方法为空间转录组的通路分析提供可解释、可扩展的工具，但与虚拟细胞建模的关系较弱。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
abstract: We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition-specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA-protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.
affiliations: Erzurum Regional Training and Research Hospital

llm.novelty_zh: 整合4444个全血转录组样本与血浆蛋白组，构建覆盖98种健康状况的资源库。
llm.summary_zh: WBT Atlas汇集了98种健康状况的全血转录组样本，并与1280名参与者的血浆蛋白组数据对照。作者联合RNA与蛋白特征训练多分类模型，在十个独立队列和UK Biobank中验证了特征。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为精准医学中的疾病转录组特征发现与跨组学分类提供了可复用的资源。

title: Decomposing multi-scale dynamic regulation from single-cell multiomics with scMagnify
abstract: Deciphering the highly coupled regulatory circuits that drive cellular dynamics remains a fundamental goal in biology. However, capturing the multi-scale time-lagged dynamics and combinatorial regulatory logic of gene regulation remains challenging. Here we present scMagnify, a deep-learning-based framework that leverages chromatin accessibility and gene expression via Granger causality to reconstruct and decompose multi-scale gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Diverse benchmarks demonstrate scMagnify's favorable performance. scMagnify employs tensor decomposition to identify combinatorial TF modules and their activation profiles across multiple time-lags. We applied scMagnify to human hematopoiesis and mouse pancreas development, where it recovered known lineage-driving regulators and provided further insights into the combinatorial logic underlying cell fate decisions. Furthermore, in the context of kidney injury, scMagnify's intercellular communication module mapped key signaling-to-transcription cascades linking microenvironment cues to pathological epithelial cell changes. In summary, scMagnify provides a robust computational framework for dissecting the multi-scale regulatory logic that governs complex biological processes in development and disease.

llm.novelty_zh: 结合Granger因果与张量分解，将多尺度时滞调控网络分解为组合转录因子模块。
llm.summary_zh: 作者提出scMagnify，利用染色质可及性与基因表达，通过Granger因果重建多尺度基因调控网络，并以张量分解识别组合TF模块及其跨时滞激活模式。方法在造血和胰腺发育数据中恢复了已知谱系调控因子，并用于肾损伤的信号-转录级联分析。

llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及因果推断的实验验证，Granger因果在单细胞数据中的假设仍需谨慎解读。

title: Mapping cell-type-specific spatial gene programs uncovers tissue architecture and microenvironment organization
abstract: The complex organization of tissues is shaped by the spatial arrangement of diverse cell types executing specialized gene programs. Cell-type-specific spatial gene programs (SGPs) are transcriptional modules that capture spatial expression co-variation within cell types. However, identifying these SGPs remains challenging in spatial transcriptomics. Here we present MacSGP, a scalable framework that integrates deep graph neural networks with probabilistic modeling to identify cell-type-specific SGPs through low-rank structures while accounting for cell type mixtures. Through comprehensive simulations and real data analyses spanning diverse tissues and technologies, we demonstrate that MacSGP effectively distinguishes cell-type-specific SGPs from cell-type marker gene expression patterns while uncovering tissue architecture and cellular microenvironments. In a mouse brain dataset, we identify replicable SGPs reflecting subregional neuronal specializations, with these genes significantly enriched for heritabilities associated with brain-related phenotypes. Across colorectal cancer datasets from various platforms, MacSGP identifies consistent SGPs that define distinct cellular niches within the tumor microenvironment.
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

llm.novelty_zh: 将图神经网络与概率建模结合，在考虑细胞类型混合的前提下识别细胞类型特异的空间基因程序。
llm.summary_zh: MacSGP通过低秩结构识别细胞类型特异的空间基因程序，并显式处理细胞类型混合问题。作者在模拟和多种技术的真实数据上验证了其区分空间程序与标志基因的能力，并在小鼠脑和结直肠癌数据中揭示亚区及肿瘤微环境生态位。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为解析组织结构与细胞微环境提供了空间基因程序层面的分析方法。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics reveals fibroblast and neuroimmune microenvironments in endometriosis lesions
abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic, systemic, inflammatory disease characterized by the presence of endometrium-like tissue growing outside of the uterus. Affecting one in ten individuals assigned female at birth, it causes chronic pain and inflammation that significantly impairs quality of life. Yet the mechanisms that drive pain and disease progression remain poorly defined. This study establishes the precise spatial transcriptomic cartography of human ovarian and peritoneal lesions, two of the most commonly found lesions. We identify shared spatial features across lesion types, including immune cell infiltration, fibroblast compartments surrounding epithelial glands, and distinct distributions of neuronal and macrophage subsets. We precisely defined sensory neuronal subtypes and mapped their spatial location relative to immune cells. We further validate the epithelial-neuronal interactome, using an in vitro 3D model of peripheral sensory brain organoids co-cultured with human endometriosis epithelial and fibroblast cells. By mapping spatial cellular interactions and conserved features across lesion types linked to pain, our study advances understanding of endometriosis pathophysiology and informs targeted therapeutic development.
affiliations: The Jackson Laboratory for Genomic Medicine

llm.novelty_zh: 绘制子宫内膜异位症卵巢与腹膜病灶的空间转录组图谱，并验证感觉神经元与上皮细胞的相互作用。
llm.summary_zh: 研究绘制了人卵巢和腹膜子宫内膜异位病灶的空间转录组图谱，识别出免疫细胞浸润、腺体周围成纤维细胞区室以及感觉神经元亚型的空间分布。作者利用由感觉类脑器官与子宫内膜异位上皮及成纤维细胞构建的三维共培养模型，验证了上皮-神经互作。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该工作为与疼痛相关的子宫内膜异位症病理机制提供了空间证据，与虚拟细胞建模的关联较间接。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: High-content morphological profiling by Cell Painting in 3D spheroids
abstract: Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. While 3D cell cultures are more physiologically relevant models - especially for studying drug perturbations - they remain challenging to image because light scatters before it reaches the cultures' interior. Here, we introduce a scalable method to adapt Cell Painting for 3D spheroids. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. By profiling 52 clinically relevant drugs, we show that single-cell fingerprints clustered by biological pathway and resolved drug effects more robustly than those of flattened spheroid-wide views. Notably, the effect of two drugs, 5-fluorouracil and olaparib, nearly indistinguishable in 2D monolayers, diverged in spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

llm.novelty_zh: 结合组织透明化与自动对焦，使 Cell Painting 能在完整球体内实现单细胞水平成像。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究通过组织透明化和自动对焦方法，将 Cell Painting 适配到三维球体，实现球体内单细胞水平的形态分析。作者对 52 种临床相关药物进行了谱分析，发现单细胞指纹比整体视图更稳健地反映药物效应，并以 DNA 损伤、细胞周期和基因表达实验佐证了 5-氟尿嘧啶与奥拉帕利在球体中的差异。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为三维培养模型中的高内涵表型药物筛选提供了更接近生理的实验平台。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: ITLN1 suppresses colorectal cancer progression by orchestrating neutrophil maturation and spatial organization
abstract: Epithelial-derived intelectin-1 (ITLN1) is frequently downregulated in colorectal cancer, but whether it actively shapes anti-tumor immunity remains unclear. We integrate multiplex immunohistochemistry, spatial analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, chromatin-accessibility profiling, and perturbation models to define how ITLN1 regulates neutrophil maturation and spatial anti-tumor immunity. In treatment-naïve human colorectal cancer, higher ITLN1 expression associates with greater neutrophil infiltration, shorter distances between mature S100A9+CXCR2+ neutrophils and ITLN1+ tumor epithelial cells, and improved survival. In mouse colorectal cancer models, Itln1 silencing accelerates tumor growth and metastasis, impairs CXCR2+CD101+ mature neutrophil generation and tumor recruitment, and promotes LTF+S100A9+ immature neutrophil accumulation in hypoxic regions. Mechanistically, ITLN1 activates a JAK1/STAT3-associated C/EBPδ program that drives terminal granulopoiesis and CXCR2-dependent tumor homing, while recombinant ITLN1 restores neutrophil maturation and tumor-killing activity. Here, we reveal a cross-tissue ITLN1-STAT3/C/EBPδ-CXCR2 axis that links epithelial ITLN1 to bone marrow granulopoiesis, coordinating distal neutrophil maturation, mobilization and spatial organization in colorectal cancer.
affiliations: Guangzhou Women and Children Medical Center
State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China
Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University

llm.novelty_zh: 揭示上皮ITLN1通过JAK1/STAT3-C/EBPδ程序驱动骨髓粒细胞生成和中性粒细胞归巢的跨组织轴。
llm.summary_zh: 研究结合多重免疫组化、空间分析、单细胞转录组和染色质可及性数据，并在小鼠结直肠癌模型中进行Itln1沉默实验。结果显示ITLN1促进成熟中性粒细胞生成与肿瘤浸润，重组ITLN1可恢复中性粒细胞成熟和杀伤活性。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 阐明上皮分泌蛋白调控抗肿瘤免疫的机制，提示ITLN1可能是结直肠癌免疫治疗的潜在靶点。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及人类队列的具体样本量，也未说明计算模型在其中的贡献。

title: Recommendation system-inspired learning of crossmodal interaction patterns between chromatin accessibility and gene expression
abstract: Despite the growing availability of crossmodal single-cell sequencing, existing approaches are limited by underutilization of biological attributes, sparse modality signals, and insufficient modeling of regulatory interactions, limiting generalization in data-scarce settings and the discovery of peak-gene-level relationships. Interestingly, such challenges mirror those in recommendation systems, where side information, high sparsity, binary interactions, and cold start problems are extensively studied. Inspired by recommender models that infer user-item preferences from incomplete interaction graphs, we present CrossRec, which reformulates scATAC and scRNA data as an interaction graph to learn regulatory patterns across single-cell tasks. Its biologically-driven bipartite graph transformer learns interpretable attention over ATAC-RNA pairs. CrossRec outperforms existing methods across various tasks, remains robust under data-scarce settings, generalizes to unseen cell types and datasets, and enhances prior-based methods. Its learned regulatory maps provide cell- and cell-type-specific insights, resolving dynamic regulatory rewiring during cortical neurogenesis and perturbation-specific rewiring of drug-induced regulation in melanoma resistance.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

llm.novelty_zh: 把scATAC与scRNA数据重构为交互图，借鉴推荐系统处理稀疏与冷启动的思路，用二部图Transformer学习ATAC-RNA配对的调控注意力。
llm.summary_zh: CrossRec将单细胞ATAC与RNA数据视为交互图，通过生物学驱动的二部图Transformer学习调控模式，并输出可解释的peak-gene注意力。摘要称其在多项任务上优于现有方法，在数据稀缺和未见细胞类型上保持稳健，并能刻画皮层神经发生和黑色素瘤耐药中的动态调控重连。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为从单细胞多组学推断细胞类型特异的调控关系提供了新的建模视角，与虚拟细胞中的调控建模相关。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及具体基线设置、计算成本与外部验证。

title: Multi-omics profiling of primary human B cells activated via distinct stimuli
abstract: B cells are central for immunity and immune-mediated diseases (IMD), but how distinct signaling pathways drive diverse activation responses over time is not comprehensively understood. Here, we obtain peripheral blood B cells from 27 female healthy donors for in vitro stimulation, profiling the response at multiple time points using RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq with surface protein markers (CITE-seq), and ATAC-seq. Using diverse stimuli including activation of the B cell receptor (BCR), Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7), TLR9, CD40, and differentiation into double negative 2 (DN2) IgD – CD27 – CD11c + CD21 – B cells, our analyses uncover activation-dependent B cell states, stimulation-specific transcription factors and regulatory regions, the dynamic response of IMD-associated gene expression, and specific open chromatin regions associated with IMD genetic risk. Furthermore, we also identify a lupus risk variant in an enhancer regulating TNFSF4 expression. The analysis data can be accessed via an interactive browser: https://mgalab.shinyapps.io/bcellactivation. Our findings underscore how profiling the full breadth of B cell activation pathways may be important for understanding B cell biology in health and disease.
affiliations: Institute of Infectious Disease and Molecular Medicine
Berlin Institute of Health at Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin

llm.novelty_zh: 在多个刺激和时间点上联合RNA-seq、CITE-seq与ATAC-seq，描绘B细胞活化的状态与调控区域变化。
llm.summary_zh: 研究从27名健康女性供体获取外周血B细胞，用BCR、TLR7、TLR9、CD40刺激并诱导DN2分化，在多时间点进行RNA-seq、CITE-seq和ATAC-seq。作者鉴定了活化依赖的细胞状态、刺激特异的转录因子以及与免疫介导疾病风险相关的开放染色质区域。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为理解免疫相关疾病风险位点在B细胞活化中的作用提供了多组学参考数据。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及仅纳入女性供体可能带来的局限，也未说明功能验证的范围。

title: Evolutionary remodeling of the ventral retina enables aerial vision in the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps
abstract: The emergence of evolutionary novelties remains a central challenge in biology, particularly for complex organs such as the vertebrate eye. Here, we use the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps to investigate adaptation to simultaneous aerial and aquatic vision. Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics reveal that the ventral retina, which processes aerial light, is developmentally expanded and exhibits region-specific opsin expression. Ventral PR1 cones express opn1mw2 rather than the longer-wavelength-sensitive opn1lw paralogs expressed dorsally. Machine-learning predictions indicate that Opn1mw2 is red-shifted relative to Opn1mw1 but remains blue-shifted relative to dorsal Opn1lw pigments. Dorsal-ventral patterning markers further reveal an overrepresentation of ventral retinal identities. Comparative spatial profiling of developing and adult Anableps and killifish indicates dorsal displacement of the retinal boundary, producing a proportionally larger ventral domain. Thus, Anableps evolved aerial vision through developmental expansion of the ventral retina and regional reconfiguration of opsin expression within conserved cone subtypes.

llm.novelty_zh: 通过单核与空间转录组揭示四眼鱼腹侧视网膜的发育扩张与视蛋白表达重排，解释其水空两栖视觉的演化机制。
llm.summary_zh: 研究使用单核和空间转录组分析四眼鱼的视网膜，发现负责空中光线的腹侧视网膜发育扩张并表达特定视蛋白opn1mw2。作者结合机器学习预测视蛋白吸收峰，并与killifish比较发现视网膜边界的背侧位移。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为脊椎动物新颖感觉功能的演化提供了发育与分子层面的解释，具有进化生物学意义。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及机器学习预测的视蛋白吸收峰是否经过实验验证。

title: Spatially resolved host and microbiota RNA profiling in the mouse gut using microDBiT
abstract: Hosts and their microbiomes coexist in a shared environment, engaging in dynamic interactions that are essential to maintaining health and modulating disease processes. To fully understand these interactions, spatially resolved and unbiased approaches are needed to map gene expression from both host and microbial cells within their native tissue context. Here, we present microDBiT, a spatial transcriptomic platform that enables simultaneous, high-resolution profiling of host and bacterial RNAs, including both mRNA and rRNA. Using microDBiT, we mapped the spatial distribution of host and microbial transcripts in the ileum and colon of germ-free mice, gnotobiotic mice colonized with a defined gut microbial community, and specific pathogen-free mice treated with dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) to induce colitis. We observed location-specific transcriptomic alterations in both host and bacterial cells in response to colonization and during inflammation. These results demonstrate the utility of microDBiT for dissecting host-microbiome interactions at high resolution and provide new insights into immune responses, spatial microbial localization, and microbiome-associated disease processes.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出可同时捕获宿主与细菌 mRNA 及 rRNA 的空间转录组平台 microDBiT。
llm.summary_zh: microDBiT 是一种空间转录组技术，可在同一组织切片中同时检测宿主与细菌的 RNA。作者在无菌小鼠、定植小鼠及 DSS 诱导结肠炎小鼠的回肠和结肠中验证了其空间映射能力。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该技术有助于在组织原位研究宿主与微生物的相互作用，属于湿实验技术进展，与虚拟细胞建模没有直接关联。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics with high sensitivity
abstract: The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. In the last couple of years, the spatial resolution for the capture addresses has been improved from ~100 μm to <1 μm, well below the size of a mammalian cell. However, the capture efficiency of sequencing-based methods is generally low, which diminishes the effect of high capture resolution and negatively impacts subsequent data interpretation. Here, we introduce a spatial transcriptomic system, which provides ~1 μm capture resolution and a much higher capture efficiency. We demonstrate that as high as ~14,000 UMIs can be captured from mouse testis sample per 10 × 10 μm² area at a sequencing saturation of 0.43. Rare cells organized in single-cell-layers can be recovered when the data was analyzed at an effective resolution of 2 μm.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出基于测序的空间转录组系统，实现约1微米捕获分辨率并显著提高捕获效率。
llm.summary_zh: 研究报告一种基于测序的空间转录组系统，捕获分辨率约1微米，并在小鼠睾丸样本中展示了每10×10微米面积约14000个UMI的捕获量。作者称在2微米有效分辨率下可回收排列为单层的稀有细胞。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 更高的捕获效率有助于在细胞尺度获得更可靠的空间表达数据，对组织研究有基础性价值。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: CPRISP: an interpretable deep learning framework predicting circRNA-RBP interactions and guiding therapeutic discovery in neurodegeneration
abstract: Circular RNAs regulate gene expression through interactions with ribonucleic acid binding proteins, but their binding sites remain difficult to predict across proteins and cellular contexts. Existing methods often focus on transcript features while making limited use of protein-specific information and structural context. Here, we show that an integrated deep learning framework combining circular transcript sequence composition, physicochemical properties, secondary structure, pretrained representations and protein features improves interaction-site prediction across 37 benchmark datasets and generalizes across cell lines; model interpretation recovers conserved single-stranded sequence patterns, while analyses of proteins linked to Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis identify recurrent pathways involving nucleocytoplasmic transport, lysosomal signaling and guanosine triphosphatase activity and prioritize compounds for experimental follow-up, supporting accurate and interpretable mapping of circular ribonucleic acid protein interactions without implying therapeutic efficacy.
affiliations: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

llm.novelty_zh: 将序列、理化性质、二级结构、预训练表征与蛋白特征整合，用于预测 circRNA-RBP 结合位点。
llm.summary_zh: CPRISP 是一种可解释深度学习框架，融合环状 RNA 序列组成、理化性质、二级结构、预训练表征及蛋白特征，预测 circRNA 与 RBP 的相互作用位点。作者在 37 个基准数据集上评估该模型，并分析了与神经退行性疾病相关蛋白的通路。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该工作为环状 RNA 结合关系预测提供了可解释工具，并给出神经退行性疾病相关的候选线索，但与虚拟细胞建模的关联较弱。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未明确给出候选化合物的实验验证结果，且声明其不代表治疗效果。

title: Neuromics: biomarkers discovery to precision diagnostics in neurotrauma
abstract: Neurotrauma remains clinically challenging due to heterogeneous biology and evolving injury cascades. Traditional severity-based classifications fail to capture underlying molecular complexity. Neuromics combines genomic, transcriptomics, proteomic, metabolomic, lipidomics, EV-omics, and single-cell technologies into systems framework to enable endotype discovery and AI-driven stratification. We address modelling challenges, promote agent-driven multi-paradigm methods that go beyond steady-state assumptions, and advocate for targeted therapeutics, repositioning neurotrauma care as predictive, mechanism-informed, and personalised clinical management.
affiliations: Institute of Nuclear Medicine & Allied Sciences

llm.novelty_zh: 提出整合多组学与单细胞技术的神经创伤系统框架，但未给出新的方法。
llm.summary_zh: 该综述讨论神经创伤异质性，提出结合基因组、转录组、蛋白组、代谢组及单细胞等技术的系统框架。作者倡导基于智能体的多范式建模，以推动预测性、个体化的临床管理。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为神经创伤生物标志物发现与精准分层提供了概念性路线图。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要为综述性质，未提供实验验证或定量结果。

title: 3D tissue model to patient atlas: dynamic network topology reveals PDAC chemoresistance bottlenecks
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) develops chemoresistance through dynamic cell-state transitions, yet the regulatory network architecture governing drug-tolerant states remains poorly characterised, because static expression snapshots cannot capture how interaction topology evolves along treatment-induced trajectories. We established a 3D PANC-1 tissue model on decellularised porcine intestinal matrix, which reaches patient-like proliferation indices and tissue-niche-specific drug responses, and performed single-cell RNA sequencing across four conditions: control, gemcitabine (GEM), TGF-β1, and their combination. Coupling pseudotime trajectory inference to dynamic protein-protein interaction network analysis, we tracked betweenness centrality continuously across cell-state transitions rather than comparing discrete states. GEM survivors engaged a proliferative programme (E2F1, CDK1, AURKA, TPX2, TOP2A, BIRC5), whereas TGF-β1 induced an independent EMT attractor (SPOCK1, MBOAT2, COL5A1, THBS1, FN1). Where the two converged, an emergent bottleneck appeared: CDK1 betweenness centrality spiked selectively, restrained by CDKN1A (p21) and WEE1, defining an S-phase-persistence state enriched for GEM survivors. Cross-examination in a PDAC atlas of 726,107 cells from 231 patients showed 8.7-fold metastatic enrichment of triple-positive cells. This framework, linking controlled 3D tissue experimentation, single-cell systems analysis and clinical-scale patient data, is applicable to drug resistance across cancer types.

llm.novelty_zh: 将 3D 组织模型的时序单细胞数据与动态蛋白互作网络的中心性分析结合，追踪化疗耐药的状态转换。
llm.summary_zh: 作者在脱细胞猪肠基质上构建了 3D PANC-1 组织模型，并对对照、吉西他滨、TGF-β1 及其组合进行单细胞测序。通过伪时序与动态蛋白互作网络的介数中心性分析，识别出 CDK1 瓶颈及与吉西他滨存活细胞相关的 S 期持续状态。在一个包含 726,107 个细胞的患者图谱中，三阳性细胞在转移灶中富集 8.7 倍。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为理解肿瘤化疗耐药中的网络瓶颈提供了实验与患者数据相结合的分析框架。
llm.limitations_zh: 主要依赖单一细胞系 PANC-1 构建的 3D 模型。

title: Integrated transcriptomics identifies a high-glycolysis osteosarcoma phenotype and links SSR3 to stemness and chemoresistance
abstract: Osteosarcoma treatment is hampered by intratumoral metabolic heterogeneity. We analyzed single‑cell and spatial transcriptomic data from 27 patients and stratified malignant cells into high- (HGlyOS), medium-, and low-glycolysis groups. HGlyOS cells exhibited enhanced stemness and chemotherapy resistance features and occupied an early inferred transcriptional state. Using nested machine learning across datasets, we derived a 34-gene Glycolysis activity Prediction System (GGPS) as a parsimonious proxy for the Composite Glycolytic Activity Score (CGAS)-defined glycolytic phenotype rather than as an independent subtype classifier. Through a separate screening pipeline combining co‑expression network analysis, differential expression, and machine learning, followed by literature mining, we identified SSR3 (which was not part of the 34‑gene signature) as a previously unreported glycolysis regulator in osteosarcoma. Independent functional experiments confirmed that SSR3 modulates glycolytic metabolism, stemness maintenance, and cisplatin sensitivity. Our work provides a metabolic classification framework for osteosarcoma and a proof‑of‑concept tool for single‑cell glycolytic phenotyping.
affiliations: First Affiliated Hospital of GuangXi Medical University
Jiangxi University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

llm.novelty_zh: 用34基因签名近似糖酵解表型，并通过文献挖掘和实验发现SSR3为骨肉瘤糖酵解调控因子。
llm.summary_zh: 研究分析27例患者的单细胞与空间转录组，将骨肉瘤恶性细胞分为高、中、低糖酵解组。作者用机器学习构建34基因的GGPS代理评分，并通过实验证实SSR3调控糖代谢、干性和顺铂敏感性。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为骨肉瘤代谢表型分型和化疗耐药研究提供了可用的标志物与候选靶点。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及样本规模限制及在更大独立队列中的验证情况。

title: Machine learning stratification of LUAD-to-SCLC transformation states and drug-response signatures
abstract: Histologic transformation from lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) to small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a clinically important mechanism of acquired resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors, but the regulatory programs associated with this lineage transition remain incompletely characterized. We reanalyzed mouse and human single-cell and bulk transcriptomic datasets to define a 13-regulon Histologic Transformation Regulon Signature (HTRS) and developed TransRiskML, a machine-learning framework that stratifies LUAD samples into low-, medium-, and high-HTRS molecular states. Across independent cohorts, high-HTRS tumors showed poorer survival, stronger SCLC-like transcriptional features, distinct genomic features, and transcriptome-inferred drug-response patterns. HTRS captured transformation-associated molecular states that were largely independent of general proliferative activity across cohorts, although proliferation contributed substantially to the prognostic signal in advanced-stage NSCLC, where adjustment attenuated the association. A simplified 15-gene surrogate score was developed for downstream analyses, and exploratory pathology suggested a trend toward higher tumor-cell nuclear HDAC2 staining in pre-transformation LUAD and transformed SCLC specimens. These findings provide a systems-level framework for transformation-associated molecular-state stratification and prioritize candidate regulatory features for prospective investigation of LUAD-to-SCLC lineage plasticity. The framework is intended for hypothesis generation; prospective studies with documented transformation outcomes are required to determine its clinical utility.
affiliations: First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University
State Key Laboratory of Respiratory Disease

llm.novelty_zh: 定义13调控子的组织学转化调控签名（HTRS），并构建机器学习框架将LUAD样本分层为低、中、高转化状态。
llm.summary_zh: 研究基于小鼠与人类转录组数据定义了13调控子的组织学转化调控签名，并用TransRiskML将LUAD样本分为低、中、高三种状态。作者在独立队列中发现高HTRS肿瘤预后较差且更具SCLC样特征，并提出了15基因替代评分。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该框架可用于识别LUAD向SCLC转化相关的分子状态，为EGFR抑制剂耐药的谱系可塑性研究提供假设。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要明确该框架仅用于假设生成，其临床效用需前瞻性研究验证。

title: Spatial multi-omic atlas profiles early organogenesis of a Carnegie stage 12 human embryo
abstract: Organogenesis marks one of the most dynamic periods of early human embryonic development. Although the morphological features of this period have been described, the underlying transcriptional and metabolic landscapes remain poorly understood owing to the lack of an integrated spatial strategy. We present spatial transcriptomic and metabolomic maps of a Carnegie stage 12 (CS12) human embryo, co-registered with embryonic anatomy to generate a unified spatial multi-omic framework. Unsupervised clustering of the spatial transcriptomic data identified 17 cell populations covering the major organ primordia. Notably, we observed spatially separable hepatocyte- and cholangiocyte-lineage primed transcriptional programmes within the liver primordium, and detected cardiac outflow tract and sinoatrial node progenitors at CS12. Furthermore, integration of gene and metabolite abundance highlighted regional associations between transcription factors and metabolic pathways underpinning lineage specification. Our work presents a spatially resolved multi-omic atlas of a human embryo at the onset of organogenesis.
