llm.novelty_zh: 将空间转录组与代谢组共配准到 CS12 人胚胎的解剖结构上，构建统一的空间多组学框架。
llm.summary_zh: 研究将 CS12 人胚胎的空间转录组和代谢组与解剖结构共配准，构建统一的空间多组学框架。作者识别出 17 个覆盖主要器官原基的细胞群，并在肝原基中发现肝细胞与胆管细胞谱系的空间分隔转录程序，以及心脏流出道和窦房结祖细胞。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该图谱为人类早期器官发生提供了空间分辨的分子与代谢参考，对发育生物学研究有价值，但与虚拟细胞模型的直接联系较弱。
llm.limitations_zh: 研究对象仅为单个 CS12 胚胎，摘要未讨论结论的个体普适性。

title: Dynamics of human cardiogenesis and its disruption in trisomy 21
abstract: Developmental dynamics involve the specification of diverse cell types and their spatial organization into multicellular niches1. Here we combine single-cell and spatial multiomics to define 21 distinct tissue niches in the developing heart, which we use to develop a context-aware, resolution-agnostic niche classification tool (TissueTypist). Applying high-resolution spatial profiling to the developing sinoatrial node, we resolve three pacemaker cell subtypes arrayed along a linear axis. First trimester subpopulations, such as pacemaker cells in the sinus horn and sinoatrial node head region, display neuroattractant programs and interact with parasympathetic neurons via interactions that include Eph-ephrin and semaphorin-plexin signalling. Temporal trajectories map the maturation of atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes and uncover a lipid-metabolic switch and potential key regulators of cell-type identity. In the ventricle, we identify cellular and transcriptional gradients along both pseudotime and transmural axes, which provide molecular insights into myocardial compaction and maturation. Comparative profiling revealed that hearts with trisomy 21 are depleted in compact cardiomyocytes and exhibit increased apoptosis relative to euploid hearts. This finding was validated in isogenic-matched trisomy 21 and euploid cardiomyocytes derived from induced pluripotent stem cells. These early developmental perturbations may contribute to the increased risk of congenital heart disease associated with Down's syndrome. In summary, we present a spatially resolved framework of human cardiac development to enable systematic explorations of developmental niches in health and disease.

llm.novelty_zh: 结合单细胞与空间多组学定义21类心脏发育组织生态位，并提出可跨分辨率的生态位分类工具TissueTypist。
llm.summary_zh: 研究利用单细胞与空间多组学绘制人类心脏发育图谱，识别出21个组织生态位并开发了TissueTypist分类工具。作者描述了窦房结起搏细胞亚型、心肌细胞成熟轨迹，并发现21三体心脏中致密心肌细胞减少、凋亡增加，该结果在诱导多能干细胞来源细胞中得到验证。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为理解先天性心脏病与唐氏综合征的早期发育机制提供了空间图谱资源。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk
abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation at single-cell resolution is crucial for elucidating complex disease mechanisms1, but has been limited by the lack of large-scale single-cell multi-omics data2-4. Here we present single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing of 3.5 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 1,042 donors with matched whole-genome sequencing. Across 28 immune cell types, we tested 440,996 chromatin accessibility peaks and identified 243,225 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) at 100,483 peaks, 60% of them cell-type specific. Rare variant analysis identified 38,161 associated peaks, with predicted transcription factor-binding disruption implicated at individual loci. Colocalization with expression QTLs (eQTLs) from single-cell RNA sequencing data (5.4 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells)5 defined 28,834 candidate cis-regulatory elements. Across genome-wide association studies for 16 diseases and 44 blood traits, caQTLs colocalized 4.5-22.6% more signals than eQTLs alone. Cell-type-specific and tissue-specific context, distal effects and multi-causal-variant models raised genome-wide association study-eQTL concordance from approximately 16% to approximately 65%. Cell state further modulates genetic effects, with 27% of over 200,000 caQTL-cell-state interactions lacking a main effect. At the inflammatory bowel disease risk gene ADCY7, accessibility effects varied with genotype and G protein-mediated pathway activity in CD4+ T cells. A graph neural network trained on both eQTL and caQTL layers inferred peak-gene links in unpaired multiome data with up to 17.2% higher accuracy than QTL-agnostic data, uncovering 128 additional transcription factor-target pairs (22% increase). Together, these results show that genetic variants shape chromatin accessibility in a cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific manner, influencing immune function and disease risk.

llm.novelty_zh: 以大规模单细胞多组学与图神经网络结合，系统刻画细胞类型与细胞状态特异的遗传调控效应。
llm.summary_zh: 作者对来自1042名供体的350万个外周血单核细胞进行单细胞ATAC测序，并结合全基因组测序鉴定了24.3万余个caQTL。研究将caQTL与单细胞eQTL和GWAS结果联合分析，并训练图神经网络以推断未配对多组学数据中的peak-基因连接，准确性最高提升17.2%。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 提供了大规模、细胞类型分辨的遗传调控参考图谱，为虚拟细胞中的遗传与调控建模提供数据基础。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及结果在非血液组织中的泛化能力，也未说明图神经网络的具体机制。

title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root
abstract: Plant development is highly plastic, with growth and architecture continuously shaped by environmental conditions. Roots, for instance, adjust their development to local water, nutrient and soil conditions. Despite this plasticity, individual root cell types are generally viewed as largely homogeneous populations that progress along a single developmental trajectory1. Here we show that rather than progressing along a single developmental trajectory, most Arabidopsis root cell lineage trajectories exhibit a stereotyped bifid topology, as revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcript mapping. One branch is characterized by a transcriptional program that is shared across multiple cell types and enriched for genes associated with environmental responses, including abscisic acid (ABA) signalling. This state occurs reproducibly in a subset of cells across multiple cell types, independent of developmental lineage, thereby revealing an additional layer of root cell identity. It is conserved across Arabidopsis ecotypes and persists despite major perturbations in developmental identity. Moreover, it is reduced in ABA-deficient and ABA-insensitive mutants and becomes more prevalent under water-deficit conditions. Together, these findings reveal an additional layer of root cell identity that is superimposed on developmental lineage and its prevalence is modulated by environmental conditions. These results uncover a previously unrecognized source of environment-associated transcriptional heterogeneity shared across root cell types.

llm.summary_zh: 利用单细胞RNA测序和空间转录映射，作者发现拟南芥根细胞谱系多呈稳定的双分支拓扑，其中一支表达与ABA信号和环境响应相关的共享程序。该状态在多种生态型中保守，在ABA缺陷突变体中减少，并在缺水条件下增加。

title: Deep learning perturbation models can outperform baselines on calibrated metrics
abstract: Recent benchmarks report that deep-learning-based genetic perturbation models fail to outperform uninformative baselines. Here we introduce a positive control baseline and metric calibration framework, showing-across 14 datasets and 18 metrics-that common benchmarking metrics (for example, mean squared error and Pearson Δ) are frequently miscalibrated, with reduced sensitivity to measure positive model performance. Under well-calibrated metrics, we find that deep-learning-based genetic perturbation models can outperform uninformative baselines.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出阳性对照基线与指标校准框架，揭示常用扰动预测指标存在失准。
llm.summary_zh: 作者在14个数据集和18种指标上评估遗传扰动预测，发现均方误差和Pearson Δ等常见指标经常失准、对模型提升不敏感。引入阳性对照基线和指标校准框架后，深度学习扰动模型可以稳定超过无信息基线。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 修正了关于扰动预测模型是否优于基线的结论，为虚拟细胞扰动建模的评测提供了可靠的方法学基础。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及具体模型结构的改进，结论依赖所选的校准框架。

title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells
abstract: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf. In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet;CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

llm.novelty_zh: 用生成式神经 ODE 联合建模基因表达与 TF 基序活性，支持在硅中扰动并据此推断救援靶点。
llm.summary_zh: DynaVelo 是一种生成式神经 ODE，可从单细胞多组学中学习基因表达与 TF 基序活性的联合动力学，并支持在硅扰动。作者据此识别出 Arid1a 缺失的救援靶点 Ctcf、Stat3 和 Bcl6，并在双杂合小鼠中证实三者均可救援 Arid1a 杂合生发中心暗区表型。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 将在硅扰动预测与体内实验验证结合，是虚拟细胞从预测走向实验闭环的较强范例。

title: Effects of semaglutide on kidney disease in type 2 diabetes: a randomized placebo-controlled trial
abstract: The GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide preserves kidney function in people with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. Here we report a 52-week randomized trial of subcutaneous semaglutide 1 mg once weekly versus placebo (n = 106 (n = 25 women, n = 81 men)) in participants with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease. To identify kidney-specific mechanisms of action for semaglutide, we performed integrated multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging of the kidney and biopsy for histology (n = 33), alongside single-nucleus (n = 22) and spatial transcriptomics (n = 13) on paired samples with before- and after-treatment measurements. Coprimary magnetic resonance imaging outcomes (oxygenation by R2*, global perfusion and tissue inflammation by T1 mapping) were not significantly altered by semaglutide versus placebo treatment. Secondary outcomes revealed that semaglutide treatment, as compared to placebo, was associated with a significantly reduced renal artery resistive index and stabilization of the apparent diffusion coefficient, indicating prevention of fibrosis progression. Moreover, secondary transcriptomic outcomes revealed pronounced effects of semaglutide on glomerular endothelial cells, consistent with the results of spatial analyses indicating reduced numbers of immune cells in the proximity of these endothelial cells. The results from this trial indicate that mechanisms of kidney protection by semaglutide may include reduced vascular resistance, prevention of fibrosis and improved underlying molecular programs promoting endothelial cell health. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04865770 .

llm.novelty_zh: 采用多模态影像与单核、空间转录组配对分析，探讨司美格鲁肽保护肾脏的机制。
llm.summary_zh: 这项为期52周的随机安慰剂对照试验纳入106名2型糖尿病合并慢性肾病患者。主要MRI终点未显著改变，但次要结局显示血管阻力降低、纤维化进展受抑制，并观察到肾小球内皮细胞的转录变化。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为GLP-1受体激动剂的肾脏保护机制提供了临床与分子层面的证据。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及样本量较小对结论推广的限制。

title: Resolving cell–cell interaction networks and their molecular logic in complex tissues
abstract: Cells in complex organisms function through extensive interactions, yet mapping these interaction networks at scale remains challenging. Here we present CCI-seq, a high-throughput method to unbiasedly capture cell-cell interactions across a proximity continuum by combining cell clump combinatorial indexing with single-cell sequencing. CCI-seq identified known interactions and fine-grained cellular organization in mouse kidney and intestine, and uncovered aberrant interactions and disrupted spatial organization in adenomatous polyposis coli knockout (Apc-KO) intestines. Applied to human colorectal cancer, it revealed subtype-specific interactions linked to clinical classifications. By leveraging a single-cell RNA sequencing backbone, CCI-seq achieves deep transcriptome coverage, enabling analysis of molecular states arising from interactions. This functional resolution revealed that interacting cells associate with distinct transcriptional programs-driving ion transport in kidney, antigen presentation in Apc-KO villi and NF-κB inflammatory activation in colorectal cancer. Thus, CCI-seq provides a scalable platform to unveil large-scale cell-cell interaction networks and dissect their molecular and functional impacts, enhancing our understanding of complex multicellular systems.

title: Generalizable perturbation prediction
OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
abstract: Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出开源、社区驱动的端到端深度视觉蛋白质组学工作流，整合图像分析与scverse数据格式。
llm.summary_zh: openDVP整合MCMICRO、QuPath、napari与AnnData、SpatialData，提供免图像分析经验的快速流程和基于AI的分析流程。作者在三项存档组织研究中应用该框架，并提出对细胞邻域进行深度蛋白质组分析的空间发现方法。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 降低深度视觉蛋白质组学的使用门槛，属于空间蛋白质组实验与分析基础设施，与虚拟细胞建模关系较弱。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及跨实验室的可重复性评估及与其他空间蛋白质组方法的定量比较。

title: Advancing morphological profiling with self-supervised learning through comparative insights into representation learning of cellular perturbations
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) enables scalable, label-free foundation models (FMs) that learn task-agnostic representations directly from images, bypassing cell segmentation and feature engineering inherent to classical morphological profiling. We present a large-scale evaluation of SSL FMs for image-based phenotypic profiling, covering contrastive (DINO), masked-based generative (MAE, iTPN) and hybrid (DINOv2) learning mechanisms, pretrained on all unannotated chemical perturbations from the Joint Undertaking for Morphological Profiling-Cell Painting (JUMP-CP) dataset (119,876 compounds, ~1.77 million images, 7 laboratories). Here we show that top-performing SSL models outperformed CellProfiler in compound-replicate retrieval on the held-out JUMP-Target2 set (302 annotated compounds, P ≤ 0.001). DINO and DINOv2 generalized across diverse perturbations and cell types, outperforming CellProfiler with 31-37% gains in site-averaged mean average precision for mechanism-of-action retrieval on EU-OPENSCREEN Bioactives (2,464 compounds), and consistently surpassing masked-based models across all benchmarks. This study provides a systematic assessment of SSL approaches for advancing morphological profiling and offers pretrained FMs to accelerate drug discovery.

title: Foundation models unlock robust phenotypic representations from Cell Painting images
Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics.
abstract: Cell segmentation is a critical yet under-standardized step in spatial transcriptomics, directly affecting cell identity assignment, spatial organization and downstream biological interpretation. Despite rapid advances in spatial transcriptomics technologies, systematic evaluations of segmentation methods across platforms and biological contexts remain limited. Here we benchmark 11 image-based, transcriptomics-based and multimodal segmentation methods across 15 datasets generated by 5 spatial transcriptomics technologies, spanning 12 human and mouse tissue types. We introduce biologically informed evaluation metrics that quantify segmentation quality, transcript recovery, cell composition, morphology, expression purity and spatial organization. Benchmarking reveals substantial variation in performance across datasets, technologies and evaluation criteria, highlighting trade-offs among segmentation completeness, transcriptomic fidelity and biological interpretability. Cross-technology analyses further demonstrate that segmentation choice critically shapes downstream analyses, including cell-type specificity, transcript contamination and ligand-receptor inference. Together, our unified Nextflow pipeline provides a scalable foundation for standardized evaluation of segmentation and method selection in spatial transcriptomics.

title: Author Correction: Prediction of protein subcellular localization in single cells
A large-scale expert-annotated 3D image dataset of dermal tissue macrophages.
abstract: Tissue macrophages are highly versatile immune cells whose morphologies shift dramatically depending on their activation state and tissue environment. This morphological plasticity reflects their diverse origins and functions but also poses significant challenges for both manual and automated image analysis. In the skin, macrophages display particularly intricate shapes, ranging from rounded to highly elongated, irregular, and non-convex forms. We developed a deep learning-based approach for the automated identification, 3D segmentation, and quantitative morphological profiling of dermal tissue macrophages in mice, facilitating large-scale analysis of cellular volume and elongation. This allowed us to build a dataset of 3D-segmented dermal tissue macrophages, comprising 947 single cells. To ensure accuracy, automatically generated segmentations were refined using a custom-designed Napari plugin. To illustrate technical validity and potential reuse, we quantified macrophage volume and elongation in adult steady-state and five-day post-Staphylococcus aureus infection samples, showing that the dataset captures biologically interpretable morphological variation.

title: Predicting transcriptional burst kinetics from histone modifications with deep learning
abstract: Transcription is inherently bursty, and burst frequency and burst size provide mechanistically informative phenotypes that are not uniquely determined by mean expression alone. Yet it remains difficult to quantify, at genome scale, how histone-modification landscapes encode these burst kinetics. Here we show that DeepBurst, a deep learning model, predicts gene-specific burst-frequency and burst-size regimes from histone-modification profiles around transcription start sites. DeepBurst uses self-attention to learn combinatorial, position-dependent predictive patterns, with training labels inferred from single-cell transcriptome data using mechanistic bursting models. Across three human cell lines and two label-inference procedures, DeepBurst achieves consistent performance under chromosome-based splits and shows strong cross-cell type generalization. Model interpretation shows that burst frequency benefits from broader chromatin context, whereas burst size depends more strongly on promoter-proximal signals. Model-constrained in silico perturbations further identify histone-profile changes predicted to shift bursting regimes. DeepBurst therefore enables genome-wide mapping from readily measurable histone-modification landscapes to hard-to-assay transcriptional bursting dynamics, while generating testable hypotheses for future perturbation studies.

title: CellART: a unified framework for extracting single-cell information from high-resolution spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Recent advances in spatial transcriptomics (ST) have achieved subcellular spatial resolution, yet existing platforms either capture sparse transcript counts per spot or measure only a limited number of genes, complicating the extraction of comprehensive single-cell information. Here we introduce CellART, a unified framework for extracting single-cell information across diverse high-resolution ST platforms. By leveraging multimodal data, including staining images, ST data and single-cell RNA sequencing references, CellART simultaneously performs cell segmentation and cell-type annotation through integration of deep learning and probabilistic modeling. CellART is efficient, generalizable and robust, and its outputs are compatible with widely used community tools, facilitating a variety of downstream analyses.

title: Validation and analysis of 12,000 AI-driven CAR-T designs in the Bits to Binders competition.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) methods for proteins have advanced rapidly, improving structure prediction and design, particularly for de novo binders. However, most evaluations emphasize binding affinity rather than higher-order biological function. We present Bits to Binders, a global competition evaluating de novo binder design in the context of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells. Teams from 42 countries submitted 12,000 designs of 80-amino acid de novo minibinders targeting human CD20 as CAR binding domains. Designs were screened by pooled CAR-T proliferation, identifying 707 designs exhibiting significant CD20-specific enrichment, with team hit rates from 0.6% to 38.4%. Top-performing candidates were validated as individual constructs, measuring CD20-specific proliferation, expansion, cytokine production, and targeted cell lysis. We identified common design methodologies and factors correlated with DNA synthesis, expression, and target-specific T cell activation which nearly double the success rates when applied as a retrospective filter. We release this dataset as an open resource, with practical recommendations to support more effective AI-driven binder design.

title: Multifaceted role of genetic and epigenetic architecture of glucose homeostasis and diabetes.
abstract: Glucose homeostasis depends on coordinated genetic and epigenetic regulation of pancreatic beta-cells, insulin-sensitive tissues, and neuroendocrine circuits. This review synthesises evidence from over 600 GWAS loci and the primary literature published between 2008 and 2026, and emerging single-cell functional genomics, CRISPR-based perturbation screens, deep-learning variant-effect predictors (DeepSEA, Enformer, AlphaGenome), and polygenic risk frameworks to explain insulin secretion, insulin signalling, and diabetes susceptibility, converting GWAS associations into mechanistic insight and genotype-guided precision therapies.

title: Recurrent hypermotif regulatory circuits in developmental programs
abstract: During development, cells self-organize into complex spatial and temporal patterns driven by regulatory circuits of transcription factors and morphogen signaling. However, the principles that govern these regulatory interactions remain poorly understood. Here, we introduce a framework to dissect the building-block circuits of developmental gene regulatory networks and explore their integration into higher-order hypermotif circuits. Using single-cell RNA-sequencing data spanning human intestinal development, we identify five recurrent network motifs, including feedforward and feedback loops, and investigate their roles in the regulation of gene expression. Our analysis reveals distinct categories of developmental genes based on their roles within network motifs, highlighting major transitions in regulatory architecture across developmental stages. Furthermore, we model the emergent dynamical properties of hypermotif circuits, including their potential roles in regulating morphogen signaling. This study uncovers a common theme in regulatory circuits of developmental programs, emphasizing how the combinatorial wiring of regulatory motifs enables robust and diverse tissue formation.

title: System-level reorganization of gene networks underlies the nurse-to-forager transition in honeybees
abstract: Division of labor in social insects is enabled by coordinated changes in physiology, neural signaling, and gene regulation, yet it remains unclear to what extent behavioral maturation reflects incremental changes in individual genes and/or a reorganization of transcriptomic regulation at the system level. Here, we analyze the nurse-to-forager transition in worker honeybees (Apis mellifera) from a network perspective, treating the transcriptome as a gene-gene correlation system whose global organization reflects collective regulatory states. Using fat body gene expression data across five developmental time points that span an interval of behavioral transition, we construct signed gene-gene correlation networks and quantify their macro- and mesostate properties. We then descend to the level of the gene and construct microstate gene lists of interacting genes. Behavioral maturation of worker honeybees is accompanied by coordinated, nonmonotonic changes in global network structure rather than simple global shifts in interaction strength across the network. Early stages exhibit broadly positive, globally synchronized correlations, whereas later stages show increased modular segregation and the emergence of antagonistic gene-gene relationships. Despite this differentiation, networks remain fully connected with high global efficiency, consistent with a flexible small-world-like organization. Positive correlations primarily support global integration, while negative correlations act as localized, boundary-enforcing constraints. Negative correlations form a structured pattern of antagonism that is sparse and module-specific, occurring primarily between functional gene modules rather than within them. Network layouts and module analyses reveal two polarized, attractor-like regulatory states, a structure recapitulated in a vitellogenin-centered subnetwork and consistent with prior experimental perturbation studies.

title: Mast cell phenotypic remodeling toward a PD-1-positive, Chymase-negative phenotype is associated with metastatic melanoma and poor survival.
abstract: Mast cells (MCs) display phenotypic heterogeneity across tissues and disease contexts, yet their relevance in melanoma remains unclear. Here, we investigated MC phenotypic programs associated with melanoma progression using high-dimensional phenotyping of MCs co-cultured with melanoma spheroids, trajectory inference, and transcriptomic analyzes. Human melanoma tissues showed differences in MC phenotypic composition despite comparable abundance between outcome groups, with metastatic melanomas enriched for Tryptase⁺ Chymase - MCs. Melanoma exposure induced MC phenotypic remodeling, characterized by loss of lineage- and effector-associated features and increased PD-1 expression, with more pronounced changes following metastatic melanoma co-culture. Trajectory analysis was consistent with a continuum toward a PD-1⁺ Chymase - phenotype, which was detected in melanoma tissues and enriched within intratumoral regions of metastatic melanomas. Experimentally defined protein changes were used to derive two MC-associated transcriptomic signatures with opposing clinical associations, reflecting lineage- and effector-enriched versus melanoma-remodeled programs. The MC-LE signature was associated with favorable survival and interferon-responsive pathways, whereas the MC-MR signature was associated with poorer survival and tumor-associated pathways. These transcriptomic associations extended beyond melanoma across multiple TCGA cancer cohorts, and independent analysis of MCs from healthy skin, basal cell carcinoma, and melanoma showed corresponding differences in MC-LE-related features. Together, these findings support distinct mast cell phenotypic programs associated with melanoma progression and identify a PD-1⁺ Chymase - MC phenotype enriched in metastatic disease and linked to transcriptomic features of poor survival.

title: Experimentally anchored, MHC-agnostic prediction of immunogenicity and cytokine release.
abstract: Background Accurate prediction of anti-drug antibody responses remains a challenge in biologics development, as current tools primarily rely on major histocompatibility complex binding affinity, which does not capture the full complexity of immune activation. Methods We developed EPITOP™, a protein language model trained on epitopes experimentally verified via cytokine release assays, enabling direct immunogenicity prediction. This was combined with IMMUNOTOP™, which aggregates EPITOP™ outputs into protein-level scores. Results EPITOP™ achieves an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.73 on the independent test set, demonstrating performance comparable to existing methods while providing biologically grounded and interpretable outputs for immunogenicity risk assessment. It also enables identification of immunogenic hotspots. Conclusions Beyond hotspot identification, the model can serve as a surrogate for peptide-level interferon-γ-associated immunogenicity when experimental measurement is impractical and may be useful for modalities in which experimental cytokine testing is difficult, although systemic cytokine release depends on additional biological factors not modeled here.

title: Cis-TERN: a graph-based method to integrate single-cell chromatin accessibility with gene expression data to infer the pseudotime ordering of cells.
abstract: Motivation Pseudotime ordering methods computationally arrange individually sequenced cells along a continuous trajectory to infer their progression through biological processes. Chromatin accessibility at regulatory elements is pivotal for orchestrating the timing of gene expression during cellular differentiation. However, data sparsity and discrete grouping imposed by clustering-based approaches, often obscures subtle cell-state transitions and intermediate populations. Results Here, we introduce Cis-TERN (Cis-Temporally Encoded Regulation Network), a graph-based method that integrates scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq to infer a pseudotime ordering of cells. Exploiting the fact that distal cis chromatin accessibility often precedes gene activation, Cis-TERN builds a directed bipartite graph between scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq cells with edge weights determined by either proximal or distal accessibility. Through network diffusion, Cis-TERN assigns continuous pseudotime scores to all cells. Cis-TERN infers cellular pseudotime without the need for prior biological knowledge, such as specifying a root cell type, thereby enabling unbiased reconstruction of differentiation from data alone. We show that our scores align with known lineages in healthy and tumor-derived hematopoietic cells. Additionally, Cis-TERN is able to trace individual cancer cells back to progenitor cell types. Our approach establishes a framework for leveraging chromatin accessibility and gene expression jointly to learn the timing of cell state progression. Availability and implementation Cis-TERN is available at https://github.com/pawelab/Cis-TERN.

title: Inferring gene expression profiles of tumor clones
abstract: MOTIVATION: Tumors are heterogeneous mixtures of clonal subpopulations of cells that co-evolve in time and space. Apart from genetic differences, cancer clones may reside in different locations in the tumor tissue and show various transcriptional phenotypes, with specific gene expression profiles and marker genes. Computational tools that simultaneously infer genotypes and transcriptional phenotypes of clones in tumor tissues are lacking. RESULTS: We introduce ClonalGE, a probabilistic graphical model identifying cancer clone genotypes, their gene expression profiles, and spatial mapping within tumor tissue. The model proceeds by probabilistic matching of single nucleotide variant sites in spatial transcriptomics to clone-specific variants inferred from DNA sequencing data, and by deconvoluting gene expression in spatial transcriptomics spots into contributions from individual clones. We propose a procedure that utilizes the Monte Carlo posterior samples for identification of differentially expressed genes between clones, using a Highest Density Interval plus Region of Practical Equivalence (HDI+ROPE) criterion that jointly requires credible and practically meaningful effect sizes. ClonalGE demonstrates superior performance on simulated data. Applied to a prostate cancer sample, it reveals clone-specific expression patterns and outperforms its predecessor model in accurately inferring gene expression profiles and explaining spatial transcriptomics signals. Our approach advances the functional and phenotypic characterization of clonal cell subpopulations in tumors. AVAILABILITY: The implementation of ClonalGE and the data used in this study can be accessed in the following GitHub repository https://github.com/szczurek-lab/ClonalGE/. The benchmarking data alongside the intermediate results are available on Zenodo at DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20446991.

llm.novelty_zh: 用概率图模型将空间转录组中的SNV位点与克隆基因型匹配，并推断各克隆的基因表达谱。
llm.summary_zh: ClonalGE将空间转录组中的单核苷酸变异位点与DNA测序得到的克隆变异进行概率匹配，并把空间点的表达解卷积为各克隆的贡献。作者采用HDI+ROPE准则识别克隆间差异表达基因，并在模拟和前列腺癌样本上优于前代模型。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为肿瘤克隆在空间上的转录表型解析提供了工具。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: scURL: uncertainty-sharpened representation learning for single-cell multi-omics clustering.
abstract: Motivation Single-cell multi-omics clustering requires integrating complementary omics layers while accounting for their unequal reliability across individual cells. However, cell-wise reliability can vary substantially within each omics layer, causing different omics to provide reliable signals for some cells but ambiguous or noisy signals for others. This challenge is further complicated by omics-level heterogeneity, where differences in sparsity, signal distribution, and biological resolution may introduce cross-omics conflicts and bias the fused representation. Results We present scURL, an uncertainty-sharpened representation learning framework for single-cell multi-omics clustering. scURL introduces representation uncertainty (RU) and establishes its connection to clustering generalization risk (GR), enabling the derivation of cell-wise omics weights for uncertainty-aware fusion (UAF). To support stable uncertainty estimation, scURL further introduces a multi-granular calibration module (MCM) that calibrates omics-specific representations from both cluster-level semantic and local-level structural perspectives before fusion. Experiments on ten datasets demonstrate that scURL outperforms existing clustering methods, remains robust under dropout noise, and identifies biologically meaningful cell populations, as supported by marker gene analysis. Availability and implementation Source code is available at https://github.com/Yaolab-fantastic/scURL.

title: scLDM: a conditional diffusion framework for single-cell perturbation prediction.
abstract: Motivation Accurate prediction of single-cell responses to external stimuli is pivotal for deciphering gene regulatory mechanisms and accelerating data-driven drug discovery. However, effectively capturing the complex, non-linear mapping between intrinsic cell states and external stimuli remains an open problem. Results We propose scLDM, a generative framework based on latent diffusion models for predicting single-cell perturbation responses. scLDM first compresses high-dimensional gene expression into a compact latent space via a variational autoencoder, followed by a conditional diffusion process to generate post-perturbation states, explicitly guided by pre-perturbation cellular state, cell type, and perturbation type. Systematic evaluations on six datasets across diverse biological settings, spanning pharmacological stimulation, viral infection, helminth infection, genetic perturbations, and multi-species immune response contexts, demonstrate that scLDM achieves superior predictive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the model exhibits strong interpretability, as the learned perturbation embeddings show high functional alignment with known biological mechanisms. Overall, scLDM provides a robust and biologically consistent strategy for in silico perturbation screening. Availability The code is available at https://github.com/samrogers1233/scLDM and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22658164.

llm.novelty_zh: 将潜空间扩散模型用于单细胞扰动响应预测，并以扰动前细胞状态、细胞类型和扰动类型共同作为生成条件。

title: METANet: a supervised ensemble learning framework for reconstructing direct and functional tissue-specific transcription factor networks
abstract: MOTIVATION: Reconstructing tissue-specific transcription factor (TF) networks remains challenging. TF-motif-based methods often lack functional validation, while expression-based methods struggle to distinguish direct binding from indirect regulation. Integration of diverse data types is necessary to accurately prioritize likely functional targets directly bound by TFs across human tissues. RESULTS: We introduce METANet (Motif Expression TF Association Networks), a supervised ensemble learning framework that combines TF motifs, cis-regulatory element activity, and linear and nonlinear expression-derived features to predict TF binding. Applied to 36 human tissues, predicted METANet maps significantly outperform established methods in identifying direct, likely functional targets of TFs validated by ChIP-seq and gene ontology. Furthermore, METANet maps capture tissue-specific regulation comparable to existing methods, allowing the identification of reproducible gene-trait associations. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: All code and network maps are freely available at Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20614479.

llm.novelty_zh: 融合 TF motif、顺式调控元件活性与表达特征，以监督式集成学习预测组织特异性的直接 TF 结合网络。
llm.summary_zh: METANet 是监督式集成学习框架，结合 TF motif、顺式调控元件活性及线性与非线性表达特征来预测 TF 结合。在 36 个人类组织中，其预测结果在 ChIP-seq 与基因本体验证下优于既有方法，并能识别可重复的基因-性状关联。网络图谱已公开于 Zenodo。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为组织特异性转录调控网络提供了可复用的预测图谱。

title: HINN prioritizes multi-omics biomarkers associated with cognitive decline
abstract: MOTIVATION: Integrating multi-omics data for disease prediction remains challenging due to the complexity of cross-layer biological interactions and the limited use of prior biological knowledge in many machine learning models. We present the Hierarchical Input Neural Network (HINN), a deep learning framework that incorporates biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships in a structured and interpretable manner. HINN was applied to blood-derived multi-omics data to predict cognitive assessment scores, including Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale 11 tasks (ADAS11), and Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test. A biologically guided feature construction pipeline was used to integrate genome-wide association studies-derived single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), promoter-region DNA methylation, and gene expression data through Gene Ontology Biological Process and KEGG pathway mappings. RESULTS: The model was evaluated using a rigorous training strategy that separates feature selection from testing and incorporates cross-validation as well as repeated runs to ensure robustness. Across all cognitive outcomes, HINN achieved the lowest mean normalized mean squared error among the evaluated models, with statistically significant improvements over most baseline methods. Ablation analyses showed that the contributions of individual omics modalities and biologically informed connectivity varied across cognitive outcomes, with the clearest benefits of structured connectivity observed for ADAS11 and MMSE. Feature attribution analysis identified a multi-omics cascade involving SNP (rs116557230), CpG site (cg24041822), and a SOCS4 gene expression probe, which showed consistent associations with multiple cognitive outcomes. These findings highlight the ability of HINN to uncover biologically meaningful cross-omics relationships relevant to cognitive decline. Together, this work demonstrates that integrating deep learning with biological knowledge enables biomarker discovery for complex diseases. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: All code, sample data, and instructions are publicly available via GitHub (https://github.com/bozdaglab/HINN) and archived on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19197057) to ensure reproducibility and long-term accessibility.

llm.novelty_zh: 在多组学神经网络中引入基于GO与KEGG通路的结构化连接，用于认知评分预测和生物标志物发现。
llm.summary_zh: HINN将SNP、启动子甲基化和基因表达通过GO与KEGG映射构建分层输入网络，用于预测MMSE、MoCA、ADAS11和RAVLT等认知评分。摘要称其在归一化均方误差上优于多数基线，并鉴定出一条涉及SNP、CpG位点与SOCS4表达的多组学关联链。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 展示了将先验生物知识融入神经网络以提升可解释性的方式，对认知衰退的生物标志物发现有参考价值。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及外部队列验证，也未说明所发现关联是否具有因果意义。

title: Dynamic graph prior-guided latent adaptation for generalizable single-cell perturbation response prediction
abstract: MOTIVATION: Predicting transcriptional responses to drug perturbations in unseen cellular contexts is a central challenge in single-cell perturbation modeling. This challenge creates a need for models that combine flexible state transitions with structured biological prior knowledge. Existing data-driven models often struggle to generalize across unseen cell types, while many prior-based models rely on static biological graphs without explicitly conditioning prior influence on perturbation-specific target support. RESULTS: We propose DGP-LA, a dynamic graph-prior latent adaptation framework that refines biological priors and injects them as gated latent corrections within a cell-state-conditioned transition model. DGP-LA couples a transition backbone with perturbation-conditioned sparse graph refinement. It propagates gene-aligned target support over the refined graph and selectively injects the resulting topology-aware signal into the hidden representation. On Tahoe and NeurIPS, DGP-LA improves Pearson Delta relative to State by 8.7% and 35.8% for generalization across unseen cell types. In zero-shot drug perturbation response prediction on unseen cell types, it improves Pearson Delta relative to CRISP by 79.1% and 67.6%. The model also improves DE-gene recovery, response discrimination, and Hallmark pathway recovery, supporting adaptive latent integration of biological priors for more generalizable and biologically interpretable perturbation modeling. AVAILABILITY: DGP-LA's source code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/bieyl/DGP-LA and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22155398.

llm.summary_zh: DGP-LA 将细胞状态条件的过渡骨干与扰动条件的稀疏图精炼相结合，以门控潜空间修正的方式注入生物先验。作者在 Tahoe 和 NeurIPS 数据上报告相对 State 的 Pearson Delta 提升，并在未见细胞类型的零样本药物扰动预测中优于 CRISP。

title: scChronos: hierarchical temporal context learning for missing snapshot prediction in single-cell time series
abstract: MOTIVATION: Single-cell time-series atlases provide discrete cross-sectional snapshots of continuous developmental processes, making missing-snapshot prediction essential for reconstructing trajectories and dynamic programs. However, destructive scRNA-seq profiling prevents tracking the same cells across time, yielding unpaired population snapshots and making missing-snapshot prediction challenging. Existing methods typically rely on explicit dynamical propagation or transport-based coupling between snapshots, which may ignore the statistical constraints of the overall population distribution and be sensitive to sampling noise and cell-to-cell variability. RESULTS: We introduce scChronos, a hierarchical temporal context learning framework that formulates missing-snapshot prediction as target-conditioned population distribution prediction rather than individual-cell propagation. Unlike cell-centric propagation approaches, scChronos explicitly captures dual-level dynamics: (i) within each observed snapshot, scChronos compresses cell populations into cluster-representative cell representations with a transcriptomic encoder, preserving population information while reducing noise and (ii) across reference snapshots, the dual-branch temporal context integration module fuses information from all available and nearby time points into a temporal representation, which is then decoded with learnable cell-generation seeds to predict the target distribution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that scChronos improves both interpolation-style recovery and extrapolation-style forecasting compared with state-of-the-art methods. Beyond reducing distributional discrepancy, scChronos better preserves developmental topology and maintains cell-type-specific marker and pathway programs. AVAILABILITY: The code and data are available at https://github.com/yjs193/scChronos and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20933283.

title: Starlng: STability Analysis of coRegulated ‘Nests’ of Genes
abstract: MOTIVATION: Single-cell assays (both single and multi-omics) represent the state-of-the-art for detailed characterization of cell phenotypes, a task frequently initialized with the identification of groups of genes linked to well-defined, stable subpopulations of cells. Gene expression covariation patterns are simplified precursors of Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) and play a crucial role in inferring causality and dynamics within GRNs. However, current gene clustering methods struggle to capture spatial organization and relationship dynamics along developmental trajectories, while remaining vulnerable to noise and algorithmic stochasticity. RESULTS: Expanding on the ClustAssess framework, which shifted the cluster-centric assessment of populations of cells to an element-centric perspective, we propose to assess the covariation induced by gene graph clustering. The Starlng (abbrev) framework provides an optimized, interactive environment for the identification of the filtered modules. The pipeline identifies the stable configuration of clustering parameters and robust gene modules (nests of genes), followed by the removal of the outlier clusters based on the pseudotime variance. We illustrate Starlng on the identification of reliable, reproducible communities of genes, as well as reveal unbiased hierarchical relationships between higher level cell clusters and more granular subgroups of genes. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: Starlng is implemented in R and freely available at https://github.com/Core-Bioinformatics/Starlng.

llm.novelty_zh: 将 ClustAssess 的元素中心稳定性评估用于基因图聚类，并结合伪时间方差去除离群模块。
llm.summary_zh: Starlng 是以 R 语言实现的交互式流程，用于识别共调控基因模块（nests of genes）。它在元素中心的稳定性评估框架上搜索稳定的聚类参数，并基于伪时间方差去除离群簇。作者用其识别了可复现的基因群落，并揭示了细胞簇与基因亚群之间的层级关系。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为从单细胞数据中提取稳健基因模块提供了可复用的软件工具。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: TRACER: twin-contrastive learning for fine-grained and rare spatial domain identification in spatial transcriptomics
abstract: MOTIVATION: Fine-grained and rare spatial domains are difficult to identify in spatial transcriptomics because they contain few spots, show subtle transcriptional differences, and are strongly influenced by neighboring regions. RESULTS: We present TRACER, a twin-contrastive learning framework that integrates a graph convolutional autoencoder with neighborhood-aware instance-level and cluster-level contrastive learning. By jointly preserving local spatial continuity and enhancing domain separability, TRACER achieved competitive and generally robust performance compared with representative spatial domain identification methods across multiple spatially resolved transcriptomic datasets, including human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex generated by 10× Visium, mouse brain datasets generated by STARmap, osmFISH, and BARISTAseq, and human breast cancer. TRACER recovered major cortical and anatomical structures, improved the identification of rare or transitional domains in the mouse somatosensory cortex, and revealed candidate functionally distinct small domains within a broadly annotated breast cancer region. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code of TRACER is available at https://github.com/luxin-heart/TRACER.
affiliations: Henan University of Economic and Law

llm.novelty_zh: 将图卷积自编码器与邻域感知的双层对比学习结合，用于稀有空间域识别。
llm.summary_zh: TRACER 是用于空间转录组空间域识别的双重对比学习框架，结合图卷积自编码器与邻域感知的实例级和聚类级对比学习。作者在多个空间转录组数据集上与代表性方法比较，并报告其对稀有或过渡区域的识别效果。

title: Single-cell CRISPR perturbation in human adipocytes reveals an omnigenic core remodeling network linking CAD loci to cardiometabolic risk
abstract: Background Genome- and transcriptome-wide association studies have identified numerous coronary artery disease (CAD) loci enriched in adipose tissue, yet their functional convergence remains unclear. The omnigenic model predicts that peripheral genes influence disease through shared core regulatory networks. Purpose We aim to determine whether genetically prioritized CAD adipose genes converge on common transcriptional programs and core genes relevant to cardiometabolic disease. Methods We established an arrayed dual-guide CRISPR-Cas9 Perturb-seq platform in human Simpson-Golabi-Behmel Syndrom (SGBS) preadipocytes. 12 CAD-prioritized genes and two positive controls, in total 14 were individually targeted. After adipogenic differentiation, single-cell RNA sequencing with gene-specific-sgRNA capture was performed. Differential expression, pathway enrichment, core gene identification, drug interaction annotation, and phenome-wide association (PheWAS) analyses were conducted to define convergent transcriptional programs and their cardiometabolic relevance. Results Eleven of 14 perturbation lines converged on a dominant transcriptional axis marked by suppression of adipogenesis and activation of epithelial mesenchymal transition (EMT). These lines showed coordinated downregulation of mature adipocyte markers (ADIPOQ, FABP4, PLIN1) and robust induction of extracellular matrix and epithelial–mesenchymal transition genes (COL1A1, COL1A2, FN1, LOX), together with inflammatory pathways. Core gene analysis identified 44 genes differentially expressed in at least 11 perturbation groups, defining a shared adipocyte ‘core’ network. Core genes displayed coherent directionality across independent knockouts, supporting structured convergence consistent with the omnigenic framework. Compared with the originally targeted genes, core genes exhibited a markedly higher number of curated and known drug–gene interactions, indicating greater translational tractability at the network level. PheWAS integration demonstrated that 28 of the core genes were associated with cardiometabolic traits, and 18 showed consistent protective or detrimental effects across metabolic phenotypes. Thus, the experimentally defined remodeling program aligns with genetically inferred disease directionality. Conclusion Most genetically prioritized adipose CAD genes converge on an omnigenic core transcriptional network in human adipocytes. In 11 of 14 perturbations, diverse loci induced a shared shift from metabolic adipocyte programs toward a pro-fibrotic, EMT-like state. Enrichment of druggable interactions and coherent cardiometabolic PheWAS signals among core genes highlights network-level regulators as key mediators of polygenic CAD risk and potential therapeutic targets.Figure

llm.novelty_zh: 将双sgRNA的Perturb-seq平台应用于SGBS前脂肪细胞，检验CAD风险基因是否汇聚到共同核心网络，属于已有技术的应用。
llm.summary_zh: 研究在人SGBS前脂肪细胞中构建双sgRNA的Perturb-seq平台，对14个基因（含12个CAD优先基因和2个阳性对照）进行单细胞CRISPR扰动，并在脂肪分化后完成单细胞测序。分析聚焦差异表达、通路富集与核心基因识别，以检验CAD脂肪基因的功能汇聚性。

title: scTraitReg: a single-cell multi-omic database of trait-relevant transcription factor eRegulons
abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) identify loci associated with human diseases and disease-related traits, but the regulators and cellular contexts linked to these signals remain difficult to resolve. We present scTraitReg, a database of trait-relevant transcription factor (TF) eRegulons-TFs with their target genes and linked cis-regulatory regions-at single-cell resolution. scTraitReg integrates 655 sets of curated GWAS summary statistics covering 122 Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) disease terms with 111 human single-cell multi-omic datasets profiling RNA and chromatin accessibility in the same cells. The resource spans 34 tissues, 252 cell types, 2 081 538 cells, and 2208 curated GWAS-single-cell analysis pairs. Across these analyses, it contains 2 840 939 TF-cell-type records for 886 regulators; 67 666 records met all three criteria-cell-type specificity, genetic relevance, and the trait-associated regulon score-and were included as candidate trait-relevant eRegulon records. Each record links to the TF-target regulatory network with its cis-regulatory regions, cell-type-resolved evidence, per-cell regulon module scores, and target-gene enrichment, all available as downloadable tables. Users can search by disease, tissue, cell type, or regulator and examine these associations through interactive visualizations. scTraitReg thus provides a searchable and reusable resource linking genetic associations to cell-type-specific regulatory programs, and is freely available at https://www.sctraitreg.bio/.
affiliations: Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University

llm.novelty_zh: 将655组GWAS汇总统计与单细胞多组学数据联结，构建了性状相关的转录因子eRegulon数据库。
llm.summary_zh: scTraitReg整合了655组GWAS汇总统计与111个单细胞多组学数据集，覆盖122个MeSH疾病术语和252种细胞类型。数据库给出了67666条同时满足细胞类型特异性、遗传相关性和调控子得分的候选性状相关eRegulon记录，并提供可检索和下载的结果。

title: EvoNiche: a comprehensive database for dissecting tumor niche dynamics and spatiotemporal evolution within the cancer ecosystem
abstract: The tumor ecosystem is organized into diverse ecological niches that undergo continuous regional remodeling and spatiotemporal evolution during tumor progression. Systematically characterizing the regional dynamics of these niches and reconstructing their spatiotemporal trajectories are essential for understanding tumor development, metastasis, and therapeutic response. Here, we present EvoNiche (https://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/EvoNiche or http://evoniche.bio-database.com/), a comprehensive database designed to systematically dissect the regional dynamics and spatiotemporal patterns of the tumor ecosystem by integrating 91 matched spatial and single-cell transcriptomic datasets spanning 35 cancer types. EvoNiche incorporates 712 tissue sections comprising 1 953 708 spatial spots and 58 single-cell datasets containing 2 945 536 cells, identifies 5609 spatial niches, and reconstructs tissue-level and cell-level spatiotemporal trajectories across tumor ecosystems. Through integrated analytical frameworks, EvoNiche enables comprehensive characterization of tumor ecosystem remodeling by resolving spatially organized cellular compositions, region-specific and trajectory-associated molecular programs and biological functions, spatially proximal cell-cell interactions, and spatial pseudotime-associated changes. Furthermore, EvoNiche prioritizes region-specific and transition genes as spatially derived candidate genes through systematic evaluation across pan-cancer and immunotherapy cohorts. Collectively, EvoNiche serves as a valuable resource for investigating regional ecosystem organization and spatiotemporal patterns across human cancers, and elucidating the regulatory mechanisms underlying tumor progression and therapeutic response.

llm.novelty_zh: 整合 91 组配对的空间与单细胞转录组数据，构建肿瘤生态位时空演化数据库。
llm.summary_zh: EvoNiche 数据库整合 91 组配对空间与单细胞转录组数据，涵盖 35 种癌症，识别了 5609 个空间生态位，并重建了组织和细胞层面的时空轨迹。平台提供生态位组成、细胞互作与伪时间分析工具，并基于泛癌及免疫治疗队列筛选区域特异和转变相关的候选基因。

title: OSCAR: an omics atlas of paired single-cell ATAC-seq and RNA-seq for decoding cell-specific gene regulation
abstract: Paired single-cell chromatin accessibility and transcriptome profiles provide a powerful framework for dissecting cell-specific regulatory programs underlying diverse biological processes and human diseases. The rapid accumulation of paired single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (scATAC-seq) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data has led to an urgent need to comprehensively integrate these data to illustrate the regulatory landscape at single-cell resolution. To address this need, we developed OSCAR (an Omics atlas of paired Single-Cell ATAC and RNA-seq, https://bio.liclab.net/OSCAR/) to curate large-scale paired scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq data and to provide comprehensive regulatory annotations and analyses. The current version of OSCAR catalogs 7749 898 human cells from 1136 samples across 30 tissue types. Importantly, OSCAR integrates paired scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq profiles for joint cell clustering and peak-to-gene linkage identification, and provides detailed (epi)genetic annotations for marker peaks and regulatory elements of marker genes, including super-enhancers, enhancers, enhancer RNAs (eRNAs), common and risk single nucleotide polymorphisms, expression quantitative trait loci, transcription factor binding sites, transcription factor/transcription co-factor binding peaks, Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)/Cas9 target sites, DNase I hypersensitivity sites, chromatin accessibility regions, DNA methylation sites, chromatin interaction regions, and topologically associating domains. Furthermore, OSCAR provides three online analysis tools, including cell type enrichment analysis, sequence-based peak regulatory analysis, and peak-to-gene linkage analysis. Hence, OSCAR is a useful platform to query, browse, analyze, and visualize cell-specific regulatory programs across diverse human tissues and diseases.
affiliations: First Affiliated Hospital of University of South China

title: SpatialRegNet: spatially resolved mapping of active regulatory network of human and mouse
abstract: The spatial microenvironment and cellular functional states are governed by spatiotemporally dynamic gene regulatory networks (GRNs), making their dissection essential for understanding disease pathogenesis and normal tissue programs. Despite the rapid development of multiple spatial transcriptomics databases, most lack systematic integration of intracellular GRNs and their spatial coupling patterns. Here, we present SpatialRegNet (https://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/SpatialRegNet/), a comprehensive database curating 1322 tissue slices derived from 152 human and mouse spatial transcriptomic datasets that span 68 tissue types and 93 distinct diseases or disease subtypes, encompassing 3 744 216 spatial spots. The database quantifies spot-level activity for 6733 transcription factor (TF)-mediated regulon networks, which collectively contain over 12.7 million TF-target gene pairs, and archives 802 935 regulon networks that are highly active in distinct spatial niches/cell types. SpatialRegNet embeds a suite of interactive online tools for analyzing regulon networks in spatial contexts, enabling users to interrogate the correlations between regulon network activity and cellular identities, map spatial regulatory heterogeneity and specificity, track dynamic regulon network activity across cell differentiation trajectories, reconstruct intercellular communication signaling cascades, and generate three-dimensional visualizations of regulon network activity. Collectively, SpatialRegNet constitutes a valuable public resource to advance mechanistic investigations of physiological tissue function, disease etiology, and biomarker discovery in spatially resolved GRNs.
affiliations: First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University

title: CellMarker 3.0: an updated resource of manually curated and computationally predicted cell markers in human/mouse and interactive web tools for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis
abstract: The updated CellMarker 3.0 resource (http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/CellMarker) offers a comprehensive resource, integrating experimentally validated and robustly algorithm-predicted marker genes for diverse cell types across human and mouse tissues. In addition, web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data are described. CellMarker 3.0 was updated with more data and new features, including (i) appending 274 tissues, 1877 cell types, 64 040 markers, and 1 245 923 tissue-cell type-marker entries over the previous version. The current release contains 930 tissues, 4455 cell types, and 90 955 cell markers, resulting in a total of 1 329 284 tissue-cell type-marker entries. (ii) Expanding the resource to include computationally predicted cell-type markers derived from six algorithms, namely Spapros, Seurat::FindAllMarkers, SEMITONES, Cepo, CelliD, and COSG. (iii) New marker information was incorporated from 168 sequencing technologies, such as CEL-Seq2 and SNARE-seq. (iv) Covering 35 types of cell markers, including protein-coding genes, rRNAs, and pseudogenes. (v) The cell tool module was comprehensively restructured and upgraded, with the original six scRNA-seq analysis modules systematically optimized and two new spatial transcriptomics modules, Spatial Expression, and Spatial Chat, added. CellMarker 3.0 is a valuable resource that integrates cell identity identification, single-cell transcriptomics, and spatial transcriptomics analysis.

title: STRAND: a comprehensive subcellular-resolved spatial transcriptome RNA architecture and navigation database
abstract: Subcellular RNA localization serves as a critical regulatory layer governing cellular polarization, local translation, and functional compartmentalization. Recent advances in high-resolution spatial transcriptomics have provided unprecedented opportunities to resolve these intracellular architectures at single-molecule resolution. However, relevant datasets are dispersed across studies and repositories, vary substantially in processing procedures and standards, severely limiting their cross-study reuse. To bridge this gap, we present STRAND (Subcellular-Resolved Spatial Transcriptome RNA Architecture and Navigation Database), a curated data resource and analysis platform for the automated harvesting, quality control, and interpretation of subcellular spatial transcriptomics data. Through an agent-assisted curation pipeline, STRAND has assembled 35 subcellular-resolution datasets from six major platforms, covering 17 tissue types in human and mouse and totalling ∼4.9 billion transcript coordinates. Building upon this standardized data resource, STRAND provides an analytical workflow spanning cell segmentation evaluation, cell-type annotation, RNA localization/colocalization pattern annotation, and subcellular compartment inference. Two case studies demonstrate that STRAND successfully identifies established RNA localization patterns in cultured cell lines and detects drug-induced RNA relocalization in cardiomyocytes. STRAND is openly available at https://strand.phasep.pro.
affiliations: State Key Laboratory of Natural and Biomimetic Drugs

title: Cell3D: a comprehensive database for interactive 3D visualization and crosstalk analysis of single-cell and spatial omics
abstract: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics yield large-scale, high-dimensional datasets. However, cross-feature integrative exploration is constrained, since most current platforms support a single data type and lack interactive visualization for multi-feature analysis. To address this unmet need, we developed Cell3D, an accessible and versatile interactive platform designed to advance integrative multi-level feature analysis. Cell3D curates 898 publicly available datasets, comprising 397 single-cell and 501 spatial transcriptomic datasets, encompassing 2 924 646 single cells and spatial spots across 105 diseases, 756 cell types, and 83 organs/tissues from 11 species. The database integrates twelve mainstream functional annotation systems, providing a comprehensive landscape for dissecting molecular features across spatial and cellular dimensions. Users can explore data at multiple levels, from gene expression and cell clusters to pathway activities and clinical phenotypes. Cell3D offers a suite of user-friendly functionalities, including customizable 2D/3D interactive visualization for dynamic multi-level feature projection, flexible data integration with automatic recognition, quantitative crosstalk analysis, and microenvironment-focused integrative analysis supporting disease research and biomarker discovery. Collectively, Cell3D enables exploration of tissue microenvironments at both cellular and spatial resolutions, bridging molecular perturbations and tissue architecture in health and disease. The database is freely accessible at https://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/Cell3D.

title: CircACVR2A (2–4) regulates stem cell pluripotency by uncoupling CDK-activating kinase functions
abstract: Differentiation of stem cells is driven by tightly coordinated transcriptional programs, yet the contribution of circular RNAs (circRNAs) to lineage specification remains poorly defined. Here, we profiled circRNA and messenger RNA expression during differentiation of human embryonic stem cells into five germ layer-derived lineages. Targeted silencing of dynamically regulated circRNAs revealed that depletion of circACVR2A(2-4), but not its linear counterpart, induced rapid loss of pluripotency accompanied by neuroectoderm-biased differentiation, phenotypically and transcriptionally. Mechanistically, circACVR2A(2-4) interacts with cyclin H within the cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK)-activating kinase (CAK) complex to modulate RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) phosphorylation independently of CDK activation, with lineage commitment consistent with destabilization of RNAPII pausing at poised neuroectodermal loci. In vivo, circACVR2A(2-4) silencing impaired neuronal migration in the embryonic mouse brain and attenuated glioblastoma progression in mouse orthotopic xenografts. Together, these findings identify a circRNA-mediated mechanism that uncouples CAK complex activity to modulate stem cell fate.

llm.summary_zh: 研究在人胚胎干细胞分化过程中分析了环状RNA的表达动态，发现沉默circACVR2A(2-4)会导致多能性快速丧失并偏向神经外胚层分化。机制上，该环状RNA与CAK复合体协同调控RNA聚合酶II的磷酸化，并在小鼠体内影响神经元迁移与胶质母细胞瘤进展。

title: scSpatial: an atlas for single-cell spatial omics
abstract: Single-cell spatial omics (SCSO) has reshaped spatial profiling by enabling simultaneous molecular characterization and spatial mapping at single-cell resolution, providing insights into cellular identities and tissue architecture within native biological contexts. By integrating spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities, SCSO datasets have been widely used to construct spatially resolved cell atlases, characterize disease-associated tissue remodeling, and map disease-relevant cell populations. However, these SCSO datasets remain fragmented across individual publications, and comprehensive SCSO resources are still lacking. Here, scSpatial was therefore developed as an atlas for SCSO with expert-curated cell annotations and high-resolution spatial mappings. The current release of scSpatial curates a large-scale collection of SCSO data, comprising over 1800 tissue sections from 630 projects generated using 16 spatial technologies; provides >20 million spatially resolved cells annotated into 173 standardized Cell Ontology types; and offers SCSO-tailored analyses and interactive visualizations, including spatial gene expression atlases, cell type distribution maps, spatially variable genes, gene expression correlations, and pathway-level spatial activity profiles. scSpatial is freely accessible to all users without requiring login at https://idrblab.org/scspatial/.

title: Integrating network medicine and foundation models reveals cell-type-specific regulatory alterations in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline and neuroinflammation. Although its molecular hallmarks are well documented, cell-type-specific mechanisms driving gene dysregulation remain elusive. While single-cell RNA sequencing resolves cellular states, most studies focus on individual genes rather than coordinated programs. Moreover, a gap persists between interpretable network-based models and artificial intelligence foundation models, which capture complex interactions but lack mechanistic transparency. Whether these approaches converge or provide complementary views remains unclear. We present an integrated study combining SCANet, for reconstructing co-expression and gene regulatory networks, with scGPT foundation model. Applied to over 1.3 million cells across 18 cell types, this approach revealed that Alzheimer-associated transcriptional changes concentrate within coherent co-expression modules, for extracellular matrix organization, immune signaling, and neuronal communication. Genes prioritized by scGPT were largely embedded within SCANet modules, indicating convergence at the gene level; however, higher-order architecture agreement was limited and cell-type-specific. Thus, scGPT highlights influential genes, whereas SCANet resolves their modular organization, providing complementary information. By integrating both methods, we recovered known Alzheimer-related pathways and identified novel regulatory candidates, including the CEBPB-CENPQ axis in vulnerable SST-GABA interneurons. This demonstrates that combining network biology with foundation models enables gene prioritization and mechanistic interpretation.

title: Unlocking the full potential of spatial omics in plants: practical challenges, solutions, and a path forward.
abstract: Spatial omics technologies provide new opportunities for plant biology by enabling molecular profiling within structurally intact tissues, revealing spatially organized cell states, developmental gradients, and regulatory interactions. While spatial transcriptomics has driven early advances, the field is rapidly expanding toward integrated spatial multi-omics by combining single-cell and spatial transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data. These approaches offer new opportunities to study development, physiology, and plant biotic and abiotic interactions in spatially preserved cellular contexts. However, despite rapid adoption, the field remains constrained by plant-specific challenges when applying technologies largely developed for animal systems. Compared with animal systems, plant tissues pose additional challenges due to rigid cell walls and diverse chemistries, complicating sample preparation, cell and subcellular segmentation, signal detection, and data integration. As a result, many studies rely on bespoke protocols and analysis pipelines that are often difficult to reproduce or generalize. Here, we provide a practical, solution-oriented synthesis of current bottlenecks across experimental and computational pipelines, highlight emerging strategies to overcome these limitations, and propose a roadmap for community-driven protocol sharing, benchmarking, and integration across spatial and multi-omics modalities. Addressing these challenges will be essential to establish spatial omics as a routine and scalable tool for plant biology.

title: A Senescence-Related Signature for Risk Stratification and Predicted Immunotherapy Response in Breast Cancer: Integrative Pathology and Multi-Omics Analysis.
abstract: Cellular senescence exerts context-dependent effects on breast cancer progression and therapeutic response through dynamic interactions with the tumor microenvironment; however, its pathological manifestations, cellular organization, and clinical significance remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated whole-slide pathology images, bulk transcriptomic profiles, single-cell ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and clinical data to systematically characterize senescence-associated features in breast cancer. Quantitative pathology and deep-learning features were extracted from hematoxylin and eosin-stained images, and a senescence-related signature (SRS) was constructed using machine-learning survival models. The SRS effectively stratified patients into distinct prognostic groups and showed consistent performance across the internally divided TCGA-BRCA subsets, with high-SRS patients exhibiting significantly poorer survival. Single-cell analyses revealed that senescence activity was predominantly enriched in epithelial and endothelial cells, whereas fibroblasts acted as major signal-sending populations and mediated enhanced collagen-related communication with tumor cells. Low-SRS tumors displayed greater immune-cell infiltration, higher immune-checkpoint expression, higher immunophenoscores, and more favorable Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE)/immunophenoscore (IPS)-based predicted response profiles, while also exhibiting distinct drug-sensitivity profiles. Integrative pathological, transcriptomic, and spatial analyses further identified STARD10 as a senescence-associated candidate enriched in tumor regions and spatially concordant with senescence-marker expression at the spot level. Functional experiments showed that STARD10 knockdown reduced cellular metabolic activity in CCK-8 assays and suppressed migration and invasion, attenuated senescence-associated β-galactosidase staining and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related cytokine expression, and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Collectively, these findings establish an integrated pathology- and multi-omics-derived senescence-related signature for prognostic stratification and characterization of TIDE/IPS-based predicted immunotherapy-response profiles in breast cancer, while identifying STARD10 as a candidate biomarker and a potential target for further mechanistic and therapeutic investigation.

title: Conditional diffusion for single-cell Hi-C data imputation and enhancement with scHiC-Diff
abstract: Single-cell high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (scHi-C) enables the analysis of cell-to-cell variability in three-dimensional (3D) genome organization, but its utility is severely limited by pervasive technical dropouts, leading to extremely sparse contact maps. Accurately identifying dropout events and imputing the corresponding missing chromatin contacts remains a challenging problem, as technical dropouts are confounded with genuine absences of chromatin interactions. Existing imputation and enhancement methods often rely on smoothing strategies or restrictive parametric likelihood assumptions, which may obscure fine-scale chromatin structures and cell-specific features. Here, we present scHiC-Diff, a conditional diffusion-based framework for scHi-C data imputation and enhancement. scHiC-Diff employs a forward process that progressively perturbs contact maps and a reverse denoising process that reconstructs chromatin interactions from noisy observations. To better capture long-range dependencies in complex 3D genome structures, scHi-C contact matrices are treated as masked images and modeled using a Diffusion Transformer (DiT). Across two complementary simulated data sets and three real scHi-C data sets, scHiC-Diff improves the recovery of chromatin interaction patterns and enhances downstream analyses compared with existing methods. Application to a developmental scHi-C data set further demonstrates improved reconstruction of chromatin organization and enhanced chromatin loop detection.

llm.novelty_zh: 将条件扩散模型与Diffusion Transformer用于单细胞Hi-C接触图的去噪与插补，把接触矩阵视为掩码图像建模。
llm.summary_zh: scHiC-Diff是一个条件扩散框架，用于单细胞Hi-C接触图的插补与增强，前向过程逐步加噪、反向过程去噪以重建染色质互作。作者在两个模拟数据集和三个真实数据集上报告其优于现有方法，并改进了染色质环检测。

title: Integration-free and cluster-free detection of localized differential gene coexpression in single-cell data with DiCoLo
abstract: Detecting changes in gene coordination patterns between biological conditions and identifying the cell populations in which these changes occur are key challenges in single-cell analysis. Existing approaches often compare gene coexpression between predefined cell clusters or rely on aligning cells across conditions. These strategies can be suboptimal when changes occur within small subpopulations or when batch effects obscure the underlying biological signal. To address these challenges, we introduce DiCoLo, a framework that identifies genes exhibiting differential colocalization, defined as changes in coordinated expression within localized cell neighborhoods - subsets of highly similar cells in the transcriptomic space. Importantly, DiCoLo does not rely on cell clustering or cross-condition alignment. For each condition, DiCoLo constructs a gene graph using Optimal Transport distances that reflect gene colocalization patterns across the cell manifold. Then, it identifies differential gene programs by detecting changes in connectivity patterns between the gene graphs. We show that DiCoLo robustly identifies differential gene colocalization even under weak signals or complex batch effects, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmark datasets. When applied to mouse hair follicle development data, DiCoLo reveals coordinated gene programs and emerging cell populations driven by perturbations in morphogen signaling that underlie dermal condensate differentiation. Overall, these results establish DiCoLo as a powerful framework for uncovering localized differential transcriptional coordinated patterns in single-cell data.

llm.novelty_zh: 无需聚类或跨条件对齐，基于最优传输图检测局部差异基因共表达。
llm.summary_zh: 作者提出DiCoLo，用于检测单细胞数据中基因共表达模式在不同条件间的差异，且不依赖细胞聚类或跨条件对齐。方法基于最优传输距离为每个条件构建基因图，并比较图连接模式的变化，在多个基准上优于现有方法。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为局部细胞子群中的基因协同变化检测提供了不依赖聚类的工具，在毛囊发育数据中揭示了形态发生素信号驱动的基因程序。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及计算成本以及对更多扰动类型的扩展性。

title: HetAnn: Cell Type Annotation for Spatial Transcriptomics by Heterogeneous Graph Learning.
abstract: Currently, several new spatial transcriptomics(ST) technologies have attained cellular or even subcellular spatial resolution. Effective methods for annotating cell types are essential for the growing volumes of single-cell ST data. Most of automatic annotation methods for ST data use reference single cell RNA-sequencing(scRNA-seq) data, but how to efficiently integrate spatial information from ST data and gene expression information from ST and scRNA-seq data into a unified model remains a challenge. The difficulty in integrating the single cell multimodal data is that different modalities have different feature spaces, which easily leads to cell type mismatching. In this study, we propose HetAnn, a semi-supervised deep learning method for cell type annotation of ST data. HetAnn learns ST-specific representation by cell graphs accounting for both cell-to-cell spatial distance and gene expression similarity in ST data. HetAnn employs a graph attention network to learn multimodal representation with end-to-end joint training on ST and reference scRNA-seq data. These two comprehensive embeddings enable HetAnn to remove the gap between modalities while preserving cell-type heterogeneity. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate the superiority of HetAnn compared with state-of-the-art methods.
venue: IEEE transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics
