title: Deep Learning Predicts Hematopoietic Stem Cell Aging From 3D Chromatin Images.
abstract: The functional decline of the hematopoietic system during aging affects organismal function and contributes to reduced healthspan. Quantifying hematopoietic aging holds great scientific and clinical relevance. Alterations in chromatin architecture are a well-established hallmark of aging that encode rich and informative signatures of the aging process, yet they remain largely unexplored as quantitative markers. Here, we present an interpretable deep learning approach based on convolutional neural networks, ChromAgeNet, that learns changes in the spatial features of chromatin architecture upon aging of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). We trained our algorithm on 3D microscope images of DAPI-stained HSC nuclei to discriminate between young and aged murine HSCs, achieving an AUROC of 0.77 ± 0.03. This approach outperforms classical machine learning models trained on handcrafted chromatin features from the same dataset. We then applied explainable artificial intelligence techniques, identifying chromatin entropy, peripheral heterochromatin, and chromatin condensates as predictive markers. As a proof of concept, we evaluated the potential of our model as a phenotypic screening tool for aged HSCs treated with epigenetic drugs to detect rejuvenation. Altogether, we demonstrate that changes in chromatin organization can be modeled via machine learning to predict age-associated chromatin states in the hematopoietic compartment. Our developed framework, ChromAgeNet, serves as an interpretable algorithm to unravel the intricate relationship between chromatin changes and stem cell aging, and advance high-throughput drug screening for rejuvenation therapies.

title: Artificial intelligence (AI)‐enabled RNA therapeutic design: from molecular optimization to system‐level evaluation
abstract: RNA therapeutics are increasingly moving from empirical screening towards rational, computation-guided design. Recent advances in RNA language models, generative models and structure-aware learning have improved sequence representation, candidate generation and structure-constrained optimization. However, favourable molecular properties do not necessarily translate into desirable biological performance, because therapeutic outcomes also depend on modality-specific mechanisms, delivery and exposure, molecular interactions, cellular state, immune responses and network-level adaptation. Here, we review AI-enabled RNA therapeutic design through the specific lens of the interface between molecular optimization and system-level evaluation. We compare the design constraints of siRNAs, antisense oligonucleotides, aptamers, mRNAs and translation-oriented circRNAs, and examine the capabilities and current limitations of sequence-, generative- and structure-based computational models. We further discuss the data resources and perturbation representations required to connect molecular candidates with broader cellular-response models. In this context, virtual cells are considered as approximate computational frameworks for candidate prioritization and risk-oriented system-level assessment rather than complete digital replicas of living cells. Finally, we outline a conceptual generation-simulation-feedback-optimization framework for integrating molecular design with progressively higher-level evaluation. This perspective emphasizes the need for better interfaces among RNA design, pharmacological context and cellular-response modelling, rather than relying on molecular optimization alone.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出生成-模拟-反馈-优化的概念框架，将RNA分子设计与系统层细胞响应评估相连接。
llm.summary_zh: 这是一篇关于AI辅助RNA治疗设计的综述，比较了siRNA、反义寡核苷酸、适配体、mRNA和circRNA的设计约束，并讨论序列模型、生成模型与结构模型的能力与局限。文章认为虚拟细胞应被视为候选优先级排序的近似框架，而非完整的细胞数字复制。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 梳理了RNA分子设计与细胞响应建模之间的接口，可作为跨领域背景阅读材料。

title: Spatial and Single-Cell Multi-Omics Analyses of T-Cell Subsets and Interactions in Melanoma Lymph Node Metastasis.
abstract: Melanoma is a highly immunogenic malignancy, yet responses to systemic therapy remain variable. The tumour-draining lymph node (TDLN), including the sentinel lymph node (SLN) during early regional spread, is not only a site of metastatic dissemination but also an important setting for T-cell priming and immune regulation. Conventional classification of nodes as tumour-positive or tumour-negative provides essential staging information but reveals little about their immune state. Single-cell immune transcriptomics, T-cell receptor sequencing and single-cell epigenomics now allow T-cell states, clonal dynamics and regulatory programmes to be examined in greater detail. Spatial transcriptomics, multiplex imaging, spatial proteomics and emerging spatial metabolomics add the anatomical context needed to determine where these cells and molecular programmes occur within the intact tissue architecture. In this review, we examine how these approaches are being utilised to study T-cell heterogeneity, spatial organisation and immune interactions within melanoma TDLNs, together with the emerging contribution of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted pathology. We also critically evaluate how these technologies are applied, with attention to tissue requirements, spatial resolution, molecular coverage, computational demands, scalability to archival haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) imaging cohorts and careful interpretation of predicted or inferred spatial features. By combining biological profiling with methodological appraisal, we highlight how multi-omics immune signatures may refine nodal disease assessment and guide future biomarker development, while noting that clinical translation will require standardised analytical pipelines and disease-specific validation across independent melanoma cohorts.

title: CellDiffusion: Enhancing scRNA-seq data integration with accurate inference of cell-cell association
abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type-specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. Current methods often fail to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, misaligning distinct cell populations or leaving batch effects uncorrected. To address these challenges, we present CellDiffusion, an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process to strengthen meaningful cell-cell associations in data integration. By learning a cell-cell attention network, CellDiffusion adaptively identifies corresponding populations across batches. Our approach applies cell-specific correction in data integration, generating cell embeddings that align cells across batches while preserving intrinsic cell types and developmental trajectories. We validate CellDiffusion across various datasets, including the human endometrium, one of the most dynamic and complex tissues featuring extensive cellular and molecular changes with the menstrual cycle. This framework also improves other essential analyses such as label transfer, clustering, and trajectory inference. CellDiffusion represents a powerful paradigm for accurate single-cell transcriptomic integrative analysis.

title: Clonal lineage tracing and parallel multiomics profiling reveal transcriptional heterogeneity induced by ARID1A deficiency
abstract: Transcriptional heterogeneity drives malignant progression, yet how it emerges within tumors remains unclear. By combining genetic perturbation and lineage tracing with parallel single-cell multiomics, we tracked the consequences of ARID1A loss within individual clonal lineages. ARID1A deficiency increased transcriptional variability both within and across clones, recurrently giving rise to diverse transcriptional profiles that did not converge on a common, coordinated pattern. This variability was accompanied by broadened chromatin accessibility at normally silenced loci and depended on residual SMARCA4 activity. Clones in which this variability was prominent showed no growth advantage under standard conditions but were preferentially recovered under specific environmental stresses and during lung colonization, a context dependence consistent with bet-hedging. Our findings suggest that loss of an epigenetic regulator can promote tumor evolution by relaxing transcriptional constraints and widening the range of phenotypes accessible to a clonal lineage, rather than by imposing a single fixed phenotype.

llm.novelty_zh: 结合克隆谱系示踪与并行单细胞多组学，揭示 ARID1A 缺失会增加转录异质性并以类似 bet-hedging 的方式利于克隆存活。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究通过遗传扰动与克隆谱系示踪，结合并行单细胞多组学，观察 ARID1A 缺失对肿瘤克隆内外转录变异的影响。结果显示变异增加，且在特定环境应激和肺定植条件下，高变异克隆被优先富集。

title: stPularity: Spatial Domain Identification via Purity-Constrained Louvain Clustering on Spatially Smoothed Cell Type Proportions.
abstract: Deconvolution of spatial transcriptomics data returns, for every spot, a full vector of cell type proportions, yet standard spatial domain identification keeps only the dominant cell type assignment (argmax) and discards the remaining composition signal. We present stPularity, a post-deconvolution clustering tool that operates directly on the proportion vectors a deconvolution pipeline already produces: it builds a k-nearest neighbor graph on spatially smoothed cell type proportions and applies a modified Louvain procedure whose objective trades off modularity against a normalized-entropy purity term, automatically determining the number of clusters without ground-truth labels. Its few hyperparameters are set automatically by Bayesian optimization over label-free internal criteria, so the pipeline runs without manual resolution selection. Because stPularity reads only the proportion matrix and spatial coordinates, it is agnostic to the deconvolution method and operates in the low dimensionality of the cell type panel (4-38 cell types). Across four benchmarks, stPularity improves over the dominant-cell-type baseline on three of four datasets, raising the adjusted Rand index (ARI) over argmax by 0.14-0.26. On three of the four datasets, this advantage over argmax persists or widens as the deconvolution proportions are corrupted with increasing noise. An ablation shows that proportion vectors and gene-expression principal component analysis (PCA) embeddings are complementary rather than redundant, their relative strength depending on whether spatial structure is compositional or transcriptomic. Expression-based spatial methods attain higher absolute ARI by reprocessing the full transcriptome; stPularity, instead, targets a distinct goal: recovering interpretable spatial structure from the composition vectors that the argmax workflow would otherwise discard.

title: From Bioeconomy to Virtual Cells: The Next Chapter of American Biotechnology
GenPerturb: sequence-grounded interpretation of perturbation transcriptomes using pretrained genomic models
abstract: Background Perturb-seq captures transcriptional responses to thousands of genetic and chemical perturbations, but does not directly resolve the cis-regulatory elements or transcription factor motifs underlying those responses. Existing approaches rely on indirect post hoc analyses or external epigenomic annotations, making it difficult to connect gene-level responses to specific regulatory elements. Results We present GenPerturb, a model-based interpretation workflow that fits condition-specific linear readouts of pretrained sequence embeddings to observed Perturb-seq pseudobulk expression. Because control and perturbation readouts operate on one gene-centred sequence representation, control-subtracted attribution ranks candidate regions and motif instances as computational hypotheses associated with each fitted contrast. The fitted readouts recover much of the observed expression variation between genes, whereas recovery of variation across perturbation conditions within each gene is more modest. On the single available erythroid Perturb-multiome benchmark, region rankings showed agreement with accessibility labels comparable to annotation-based scores, with slightly closer agreement in the 1–10 and 10–100 kb strata, while the perturbed transcription factor’s motif family was recovered at comparable frequencies from attribution-derived and chromatin-derived regions. Selected lineage and compound examples illustrate motif associations that can differ from those of the corresponding transcription factor mRNA. Conclusions GenPerturb transfers regulatory priors learned during external pretraining to observed RNA-only Perturb-seq profiles, producing ranked, locus-anchored cis-regulatory hypotheses without a matched chromatin assay in the target experiment. Scoped to observed responses rather than prediction of unseen perturbations or cell types, the workflow offers computational candidates for experimental assessment of enhancer and transcription-factor activity.

llm.novelty_zh: 将预训练基因组序列模型的嵌入与 Perturb-seq 伪批量表达拟合，给出可定位的顺式调控假设。
llm.summary_zh: GenPerturb 对预训练序列嵌入拟合条件特异的线性读出，并用对照减除的归因对区域与模体排序，以获得与各扰动对比相关的顺式调控候选。作者在单一红系 Perturb-multiome 基准上报告，区域排序与可及性标签的一致性与基于注释的分数相当，但跨扰动条件的变异恢复较弱。

title: TurbOmics: a web-based platform for the analysis of metabolomics data using a multi-omics integrative approach
abstract: Multi-omics integration is highly effective for the holistic characterization of biological systems. However, current bioinformatics tools face limitations when incorporating metabolomics data, particularly for handling untargeted annotation, and when providing alternatives to predefined knowledge bases. Advanced algorithms required for multi-omics integration typically demand programming skills and statistical background, restricting their use to specialized users. Here, we introduce TurbOmics, a user-friendly web-based platform that enables researchers with diverse backgrounds to analyze metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics data using an integrative workflow that includes advanced algorithms for multi-omics integration, while addressing key challenges associated with metabolomics data. The platform is available at https://proteomics.cnic.es/TurboPutative/TurbOmicsApp.html .

llm.summary_zh: TurbOmics是面向代谢组、蛋白组和转录组数据的网页分析平台，集成多组学整合算法，并针对代谢组学的非靶向注释问题提供替代已知数据库的方案。摘要未给出与其他工具的定量比较。

llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及方法基准评估、性能比较以及注释准确性的验证。

title: Mitigating bias in spatial transcriptomic pipelines via human feedback with CSDE
abstract: Biological discovery from large-scale assays requires extensive preprocessing, during which raw outputs (e.g., images, sequences) are processed into structured forms amenable to analysis. In spatial transcriptomics, differential expression analysis depends on cell segmentation, gene expression quantification, and cell-type annotation, all prone to systematic errors. We introduce corrected spatial differential expression (CSDE), building on prediction-powered inference to leverage a small set of expert-validated cells to correct for preprocessing bias. Across three case studies, CSDE yields more reliable differential expression estimates than the prevalent approach neglecting preprocessing.

llm.novelty_zh: 借助预测驱动推断（PPI），用少量专家验证的细胞校正空间转录组预处理偏差，改进差异表达分析。
llm.summary_zh: CSDE基于预测驱动推断框架，利用少量经专家验证的细胞修正细胞分割、基因定量和细胞类型注释等预处理环节的系统性偏差。作者在三个案例研究中展示其差异表达估计比忽略预处理偏差的常用方法更可靠。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为空间转录组差异分析提供了纠偏框架，有助于提升下游生物学结论的可靠性。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及所需专家验证细胞的数量要求，也未说明方法在更大规模数据上的表现。

title: CellPatch: a flexible and efficient framework for single-cell foundation models empowered by heuristic gene patching
abstract: Foundation models have advanced single-cell omics analysis but often remain too complex for practical use. We present CellPatch, a lightweight foundation model combining cross-attention with heuristic gene patching to reduce computational complexity during pretraining and fine-tuning while enabling inspection of gene-attention patterns. Across single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets spanning multiple organs and tissue states, CellPatch achieves state-of-the-art performance on diverse prediction tasks. Its modular design supports linear, adapter-based and task-specific architectures, enabling CellPatch to be adapted to diverse biological tasks.

llm.novelty_zh: 用交叉注意力结合启发式基因分块降低单细胞基础模型的计算复杂度，并保留基因注意力的可检视性。
llm.summary_zh: 作者提出CellPatch，一种轻量单细胞基础模型，通过交叉注意力与启发式基因分块降低预训练和微调成本。在多器官和多组织状态的单细胞RNA测序数据上，模型在多种预测任务中取得先进表现，并支持线性、适配器和任务专用架构。

title: Understanding cell fate decisions with temporal attention.
abstract: Understanding non-genetic determinants of cell fate is critical for developing and improving cancer therapies, as genetically identical cells can exhibit divergent outcomes under the same treatment conditions. In this work, we present a deep learning approach for cell fate prediction from raw long-term live-cell recordings of cancer cell populations under chemotherapeutic treatment. Our Transformer model is trained to predict cell fate directly from raw image sequences, without relying on predefined morphological or molecular features. Beyond classification, we introduce a comprehensive explainability framework for interpreting the temporal and morphological cues guiding the model's predictions. We demonstrate that prediction of cell outcomes is possible based on the video only, our model achieves balanced accuracy of 0.94 and an F1-score of 0.93. Attention and masking experiments further indicate that the signal predictive of the cell fate is not uniquely located in the final frames of a cell trajectory, as reliable predictions are possible up to 8 h before the event. Our analysis reveals distinct temporal distribution of predictive information in the mitotic and apoptotic sequences, as well as the role of cell morphology and p53 signaling in determining cell outcomes. Together, these findings demonstrate that attention-based temporal models enable accurate cell fate prediction while providing biologically interpretable insights into non-genetic determinants of cellular decision-making.

llm.novelty_zh: 用 Transformer 直接从原始活细胞影像序列预测癌细胞命运，并配套可解释性分析框架。

title: CardamomOT: A mechanistic optimal transport-based framework for gene regulatory network inference, trajectory reconstruction and generative modeling
abstract: A key challenge in inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cellular processes such as differentiation and reprogramming from experimental data lies in the impossibility of directly measuring protein dynamics at the single-cell level, which prevents establishing causal relationships between regulator activity and target responses. In earlier work, we introduced CARDAMOM, an algorithm that uses temporal snapshots of scRNA-seq data to calibrate a GRN-driven mechanistic model of gene expression. However, this method had several limitations: it could only rely on the relative ordering of time points rather than their exact labels, imposed restrictive quasi-stationary assumptions on protein dynamics, and depended on multiple hyperparameters. Here, we present CardamomOT, a new method based on the same mechanistic model that jointly reconstructs the GRN and unobserved protein trajectories from the data within a mechanistic optimal transport framework. By incorporating exact time labels and priors on protein kinetic rates from the literature, and substantially reducing the number of required hyperparameters, our approach addresses these limitations and substantially improves the accuracy and robustness of GRN calibration. We validate our framework on both in silico and experimental datasets, demonstrating computational scalability and consistently improved performance over state-of-the-art methods in both GRN and trajectory reconstruction on simulated datasets, and, on experimental datasets, reconstruction of cellular trajectories, velocity fields and latent protein levels that are mutually consistent, together with GRN structures consistent with known biology. We also show that these improvements make the calibrated mechanistic model suitable to be used as a generative model to generate testable predictions of cellular responses to unseen perturbations. To our knowledge, this is among the first methods to explicitly integrate mechanistic GRN inference, trajectory reconstruction, and simulation of realistic datasets into a unified framework for scRNA-seq time series analysis.

llm.novelty_zh: 在机理模型框架内用最优传输联合推断基因调控网络与未观测蛋白轨迹，并引入精确时间标签与蛋白动力学先验。

title: HiFIseek: Gene-specific enrichment of high-impact mutations in associated genomic regions
abstract: Transcription is regulated through the sequence-specific binding of transcription factors (TFs) to cis-regulatory regions (CRRs); DNA variants in CRRs can disrupt TF-DNA interactions and gene regulatory networks through a cascading effect. Despite a few cases of reported recurrent cis-regulatory variants (CRVs), another approach for detecting non-coding functional events relies on combining gene-CRR associations capturing the regulatory elements controlling gene transcription, and functional impact (FI) scores quantifying the deleterious effect of variants. While many methods exist for each, how much they agree and how strongly the choice of CRR-FI score combination impacts the prediction of cis-regulatory altered genes has not been systematically assessed. Here, we demonstrate that gene-CRR associations and FI scoring methods exhibit little consensus, highlighting the impact of the choice of a specific CRR-FI score combination in a given analysis. These observations point to the need for a systematic approach to evaluate several gene-CRR and FI scoring methods in a unified framework. To address this gap, we developed HiFIseek, a Snakemake pipeline of two enrichment detection methods exploring the enrichment of high FI variants in CRRs associated with a gene using all region-score combinations. We applied HiFIseek to detect genes exhibiting high functional impact CRVs in eight cancer cohorts and a set of breast cancer risk-associated single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). We demonstrate that cancer driver genes exhibit a higher frequency of FI CRVs compared to non-cancer genes. In the cancer cohorts, HiFIseek detected genes pointing to cancer-related pathways with enrichment for high FI CRVs despite a small degree of agreement across CRR-FI score combinations. In the SNP cohort, HiFIseek found again small consensus across CRR-score combinations, one of which returned 18 known cancer-related genes, including BRCA1, showing an enrichment of high-impact CRVs.

title: Spatial Transcriptomics As Rasterized Image Tensors (STARIT) characterizes cell states with subcellular molecular heterogeneity.
abstract: Imaging-based spatially resolved transcriptomics (imSRT) technologies provide high-throughput molecular-resolution spatial characterization of genes within cells. Conventional analysis methods to identify cell-types and states in imSRT data rely on gene count matrices derived from tallying the number of mRNA molecules detected for each gene per segmented cell, thereby overlooking subcellular heterogeneity that can be useful in defining cell states. To take advantage of the molecular-resolution information in imSRT data and potentially identify cell-states based on subcellular heterogeneity, we developed STARIT (Spatial Transcriptomics As Rasterized Image Tensors). STARIT converts transcripts within segmented cells in imSRT data into an image-based tensor representation that can be combined with deep learning computer vision models for downstream analysis. Using simulated and real imSRT data, we demonstrate that STARIT distinguishes transcriptionally distinct cell-types and further separates cell states based on subcellular transcript localization, which conventional gene count analysis fails to capture. By providing a standardized framework to encode subcellular molecular information in imSRT data, STARIT will enable deeper insights into subcellular heterogeneity and enhance the identification and characterization of cell-types and states that are overlooked by gene count representations.

title: SADRP: A structurally aware multi-modal framework for drug response prediction
abstract: MOTIVATION: Predicting drug sensitivity across diverse cancer samples is a fundamental challenge in personalized therapy and drug discovery. This task requires comprehensive characterization of both drug and cancer cell line features. Current approaches often fail to fully capture the complex structural characteristics and interactions of drug compounds and struggle to integrate multi-omics features derived from the same sample, limiting their feature representation capacity. Consequently, there is a need for modeling frameworks that can jointly model molecular structural features and multi-modal cellular contexts in a unified manner. RESULTS: We present SADRP, a structurally aware multi-modal framework for drug response prediction, designed to model complex molecular structures and multi-omics data. For drug representation, SADRP incorporates Shortest Distance Path (SDP) encoding and edge encoding to capture both topological relationships and bond-type chemical semantics. For cell line profiling, a multi-view interactive encoder integrates gene expression and DNA methylation, capturing cross-omics synergistic complementarity. SADRP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, while also identifying potential therapeutic candidates and biomarkers, providing mechanistic insights and supporting applications in drug discovery and personalized medicine.

llm.novelty_zh: 结合最短距离路径编码与键类型边编码刻画药物结构，并以多视图编码器融合基因表达与DNA甲基化预测药物敏感性。
llm.summary_zh: SADRP是一种结构感知的多模态药物响应预测框架，利用最短距离路径和边编码表示药物分子，并用多视图交互编码器整合细胞系的基因表达与DNA甲基化数据。作者报告其性能优于现有方法，并识别了潜在治疗候选和生物标志物。

llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell–to–bulk transcriptome mapping
abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug sensitivity measurements into cell subtype- and single-cell-specific profiles. We first validate CLIMB using in-vitro mixtures of leukemic cell lines with experimentally known cell-type proportions, then extend this validation to large-scale, cross-dataset pseudo-bulk analyses built from independent scRNA-seq references across two disease contexts and five cancer types - mimicking the reference-to-target mismatches encountered in real applications - and show that CLIMB accurately infers the cellular composition of bulk samples, outperforming state-of-the-art bulk deconvolution methods. We emphasize CLIMB's effectiveness in acute myeloid leukemia, where it offers highly accurate estimation of leukemic stem cell fractions across three test datasets and three patient cohorts. We then validate CLIFF, our algorithm for estimating cell subtype- and single-cell-specific drug sensitivity, first on the same in-vitro cell line mixtures using experimentally measured drug responses, and then through in-depth, realistic-scale pseudo-bulk simulations. We applied our deconvolution strategy to the beatAML cohort dataset, currently the most extensive database of ex-vivo drug screening data. This analysis generated a cell subtype-resolved drug sensitivity landscape for 121 compounds, revealing multiple compounds putatively active against leukemic stem cells, including midostaurin, A-674563, SNS-032, and foretinib. Collectively, our work introduces a general computational framework for resolving bulk functional measurements at cell-type and single-cell resolution, providing an attractive new computational tool for drug development and precision medicine.

title: Interpretable neural networks prioritize cancer driver genes from genome-wide dependency landscapes.
abstract: Identifying cancer driver genes and their therapeutic impact remains a core challenge in computational cancer biology. We introduce xNNDriver and xAEDriver, two interpretable neural network frameworks that connect cancer mutations with genome-wide DepMap gene dependencies, pathway activity, and drug-response patterns. xNNDriver is a supervised pathway-guided model that evaluates whether a gene's mutation status is encoded in the genome-wide dependency landscape; we interpret model fitness as a driver potential score, which quantifies the strength of this mutation-dependency signal and prioritizes genes with broad functional footprints. Across 3,008 candidate genes, xNNDriver recovers major established drivers and highlights literature-supported candidates, while pathway analyses reveal biologically coherent programs related to metabolism, growth factor signaling, and immune regulation. To capture combinatorial functional states, xAEDriver uses an unsupervised autoencoder to learn Driver Variant Representations (DVRs), latent binary features guided by the frequency distribution of known driver mutations. DVRs capture cell-line-specific dependency patterns and expression patterns and are associated with drug sensitivity and pathway activity. Together, these interpretable deep learning models demonstrate that gene dependency landscapes encode rich, interpretable signals of oncogenic function and provide a hypothesis-generating framework for prioritizing drivers, pathways, and therapeutic vulnerabilities for further experimental validation.

llm.novelty_zh: 以DepMap全基因组依赖谱训练可解释神经网络，并用自编码器学习驱动变异潜在表征。
llm.summary_zh: xNNDriver基于通路引导的监督网络，检验突变状态是否编码在全基因组依赖谱中，并以拟合度定义驱动潜力评分。xAEDriver用无监督自编码器学习驱动变异表征，摘要称其与药物敏感性和通路活性相关。

title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulatory links using a dual-head Transformer. These two heads correspond to complementary task objectives: a classification head for regulatory link prediction and a projection head for gene pair-level supervised contrastive learning. This design enables the model to optimize both prediction accuracy and representation separability in a sparse single-cell setting. The human-mouse shared-gene stage is used to initialize expression-derived gene representations in a harmonized gene space. During dataset-wise supervised training, GenePairSupCon is applied within each training fold to regularize gene-pair representations, followed by fine-tuning and evaluation within each BEELINE dataset. To enhance reproducibility and interpretability, we further clarify the mapping of orthologous genes and gene symbol unification, TF-level data partitioning and leakage control, negative label sensitivity, and quantitative embedding quality assessment. Hard negative example experiments show that negative label construction has a substantial impact on task difficulty, while supervised contrastive learning significantly improves the separability of embeddings, as measured by Silhouette score, Davies-Bouldin index, Calinski-Harabasz score, and inter/intra distance ratio. GP-DHT can also recover prior-supported candidate regulatory modules and provide additional interpretable support through post-hoc pair-level attribution analysis on frozen predictors. In summary, these results support GP-DHT as a robust shared gene representation learning framework for dataset-level single-cell GRN prediction.
affiliations: School of Information Engineering, Jingdezhen Ceramic University, Jingdezhen, Jiangxi, China.

llm.novelty_zh: 在人与小鼠统一的共享基因空间上预训练基因表征，并结合监督对比学习做单细胞GRN推断，属于已有框架的组合。
llm.summary_zh: GP-DHT利用BEELINE的人和小鼠数据在共享基因空间中预训练基因表征，并构建多关系异构图刻画基因与细胞的表达关系。模型以双头Transformer同时完成TF-靶基因连接分类与基因对层面的对比学习投影。

title: Embedding of differential expression data using the contrastive language-image pre-training objective
abstract: In a given cellular context, such as a disease state, transcription may be altered. Differential expression analysis aims to quantify differences in transcript abundance across genes between conditions, but the current methods for interpretation of its results struggle to generate meaningful scientific insight and barely utilize the large amounts of gene expression data generated by the scientific community. In an effort to improve the interpretability, I utilized the Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) objective in order to create a joint embedding space for numerical differential expression data and their textual annotations. As training data, I used Gemma, a database containing tens of thousands of publicly available expression experiments that have been re-analyzed for differential expression. I trained embedding models from scratch but also fine-tuned the single-cell foundation models Geneformer and scGPT, which surprisingly resulted in an increase in performance. I thereby demonstrated that single-cell foundation models are able to extrapolate information from their pre-training to bulk differential expression data despite the fundamental difference in data modality. My embeddings allow identification of biological conditions that have characteristic transcriptomic signatures.

llm.novelty_zh: 将CLIP对比目标用于差异表达结果与文本注释的联合嵌入，并微调Geneformer与scGPT处理批量差异表达数据。
llm.summary_zh: 作者用CLIP对比目标为数值差异表达数据与文本注释构建联合嵌入空间，训练数据来自Gemma数据库中再分析的大量表达实验。除从头训练外，他们还微调了Geneformer与scGPT，性能有所提升，表明单细胞基础模型的预训练知识可迁移到批量数据。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该工作显示单细胞基础模型可迁移到批量差异表达数据，为基于文本条件检索表达签名提供了思路。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未报告与基线方法的系统比较，结果规模与统计检验信息有限。

title: Hepatobiliary cancers digital twins: Integrating artificial intelligence-driven multi-omics with organoid dynamics.
abstract: Static biomarkers are increasingly failing to predict outcomes in hepatobiliary cancers, largely due to the profound heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment. Over the past decade, rapid advances in digital pathology, single-cell profiling, and spatial multi-omics have generated increasingly detailed maps of tumor architecture. Yet, these static snapshots fail to capture the dynamic cellular interactions driving disease progression. Conversely, patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and organ-on-chip models capture functional drug responses but often lack the microenvironmental complexity of the original tumor. In this review, we use the term digital twin to refer to a patient-specific model that is initialized with individual baseline data, linked to measurable biological or clinical readouts, and refined with longitudinal observations. We outline a unified three-layer architecture: A Data Layer (digitizing static atlases), a Physical Layer (engineering high-fidelity PDO avatars using tunable biomaterials), and a Computational Layer (integrating PDOs and patient data). Moreover, we discuss clinical applications, including individualized therapy selection, exploration of resistance mechanisms, and optimization of drug combinations and treatment sequences. Finally, we highlight the major barriers to clinical translation, including limited paired datasets, variable PDO feasibility, and the difficulty of integrating data collected at different time scales. Taken together, these advances may support more individualized and adaptive care in hepatobiliary cancers.

title: Pretrained foundation models versus task-specific deep learning for gene-regulatory prediction: a PRISMA 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis of head-to-head comparisons
abstract: Systematic review and meta-analysis of peer-reviewed studies (1 January 2020 to 23 September 2026) that develop or evaluate pretrained foundation models (DNA and RNA language models, single-cell foundation models, multimodal epigenomic models) for gene-regulatory prediction tasks. The review maps the evidence and pools within-study comparisons in which a foundation model and a task-specific deep-learning model trained from scratch are evaluated on the same test data. Reported according to PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. The full protocol (amendment v0.3, 12 October 2026) is attached to this registration.

llm.novelty_zh: 用 PRISMA 方法系统综述并汇总基础模型与任务专用模型在基因调控预测上的配对比较。

llm.why_it_matters_zh: 直接检验单细胞基础模型在调控预测中是否优于任务专用模型，对方法选择有参考价值。
llm.limitations_zh: 该文为注册方案，尚未给出汇总结果，摘要也未提及纳入研究的质量评估细节。

title: 扰动锚定的人类 CD4+ T 细胞衰老方向分区：v1.5 预注册
abstract: 本研究拟使用 OneK1K 供体级 CD4 衰老表达特征和原代 CD4 T 细胞 Rest perturb-seq，建立预定的 measured-gene 方向分区，并结合独立横断面队列和人群遗传资源检验。P2 纵向稳定性为探索性。登记后先进行资源可得性及预定组成稳健性检查：同一供体与基因集合中，组成调整前后年龄系数的 Pearson 相关须严格大于 0.80；不足以估计则暂停，未通过则停止进入 MR。登记前已读取 eQTLGen 汇总字段作工具覆盖计数并做纯合成模拟，未计算本研究年龄特征、实际分区或遗传验证。完整方案以 v1.4 原文与 v1.5 补充共同为准，冲突处以 v1.5 为准。

title: From mechanistic whole-cell models to AI virtual cells: a systematic evidence synthesis of predictive cellular modelling and validation (1997-2025)
abstract: This is a retrospective, open-ended registration, not a prospective preregistration. The literature search, screening, coding, and statistical analysis were completed before this record was created. The record is deposited to place a public, third-party timestamp on the study protocol, the frozen analytical artefacts, and a complete list of deviations between what was planned and what was done. It should be read as a transparency record, not as evidence that the analysis plan predated the analysis. The study asks whether the expansion of predictive cellular ("virtual cell") modelling capability between 1997 and 2025 has been accompanied by a corresponding increase in independent external, experimentally grounded, and prospective validation evidence. Full protocol, eligibility criteria, search strategy, coding scheme, analysis plan, and deviations are given in the Summary field.

llm.novelty_zh: 对1997–2025年虚拟细胞建模的外部验证证据做系统证据综合，并公开登记协议与偏离记录。
llm.summary_zh: 该条目是对机理全细胞模型到AI虚拟细胞的系统证据综合的回顾性登记，记录检索、筛选、编码与分析的时间戳以及与计划不符之处。研究问题是建模能力扩张是否伴随独立、实验支持与前瞻性验证证据的同步增长。

title: Advances in early human embryonic development and organogenesis from spatiotemporal multi-omics
abstract: Deciphering early human embryonic development and organogenesis is constrained by limited access to in vivo specimens and the intrinsic complexity of spatiotemporal cell fate dynamics. Recent advances in spatiotemporal multi-omics have begun to overcome these barriers by enabling the reconstruction of in silico human embryos and developmental trajectories with spatial and temporal resolution. These approaches have revealed fundamental principles of lineage specification, cell migration, tissue morphogenesis, and axial patterning in early human development. In this Review, we summarize how single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies, particularly spatial transcriptomics, have transformed the study of human early embryogenesis, organogenesis, and stem-cell-derived embryoid systems. We highlight analytical frameworks that integrate spatial context, temporal progression, and multimodal datasets, and discuss how biological discovery and algorithmic innovation have co-evolved. Finally, we outline how artificial intelligence, foundation models, and large-scale multimodal learning may eventually enable predictive and causal modeling of human development, while addressing current technical, interpretability, and ethical challenges.
venue: Journal of Translational Genetics and Genomics

title: Attractor Landscapes and Network Dynamics of iPSC-Derived Neural Stem Cell Plasticity: A Complexity-Theoretic Benchmark of Cell-Fate Transitions
abstract: Cell fate decisions are often studied as static transcriptomic snapshots even though differentiation is intrinsically a complex dynamical, multistable, and plastic process. To better elucidate cell fate plasticity dynamics, we developed a complexity-theoretic and machine learning framework to model neural stem cell state-transitions using a two-time point single-cell RNA-sequencing subset of GSE138121 (iPSC-derived motor neurons). The primary cohort comprised 1,960 quality-controlled cells from the Batch A control iPSC line at days 12 and 18, represented by 815 genes and 62 metacells. Ten neural/progenitor states were annotated and contrasted with NNMF and Leiden communities. We integrated forward-in-time metacell transport, quasi-potential landscapes, basin and dwell-time analysis, Spearman and Kauffman Random Boolean Networks, BDM perturbation analysis, and 5-fold cross-validation of classical machine learning and deep learning models. Transition kernels showed broad funneling toward the neuroblast/immature-neuron state. The continuous attractor landscape resolved four basins, while the 180-node, 1,080-edge Boolean Kauffman abstraction produced 18 attractors, basin entropy of 2.75 bits, and Derrida one-bit sensitivity of 1.69, indicating damage amplification rather than directly demonstrated critical point. Consensus steering prioritized ONECUT2, ZFP36L1, DCX, HOXB2, TMEM123, TUBA1A, ENO1, ELAVL4, MAP1B, and MLLT11. ESN/reservoir computing yielded the lowest latent endpoint MAE (0.138), while CTM and Transformer achieved the lowest transition-kernel RMSE after validation-selected blending with a training-only state/time prior (0.0402 and 0.0404). These results support a complex systems view of iPSC-derived neural differentiation as trajectories through a multi-basin state-space, linking attractor geometry, network topology, and explainable AI to generate testable candidates for cell fate control and reprogramming.

title: When Does a Perturbation Model Know Enough?
abstract: Single-endpoint Perturb-seq data describe transcriptional responses without identifying the biological processes that produced them. We investigate whether layerwise response predictions provide a reproducible computational descriptor of these endpoints. Inspired by Adaptive Computation Time and PonderNet, RefineRx fits an oracle-supervised halting head and a refinement token on STATE backbones with frozen pretrained weights. All eight layers execute; expected halting depth summarizes a learned distribution over layer exits and does not save computation. Reanalysis of released four-seed arrays gives mean pairwise Spearman correlations of 0.761–0.854 across K562, HepG2, Jurkat, and RPE1. These estimates include training and validation perturbations and measure stability within fitted model–data systems. In released outputs from two CD4⁺ T-cell donors, cross-donor agreement is \(-0.110\) at rest, \(-0.097\) at 8 h, and \(0.486\) at 48 h after stimulation. At 48 h, perturbations annotated as resting-sparing suppressors have modestly lower depth than damaging or other perturbations (Cliff's \(\delta=-0.162\) and \(-0.239\)), with little separation from the inflammatory category (\(\delta=-0.011\)). These exploratory comparisons use preassigned transcriptomic labels and do not establish therapeutic effects. The results support expected layer-exit depth as a stable model-conditioned descriptor in the evaluated settings, without establishing biological complexity, causal depth, predictive superiority, or generalization to new donors.

llm.novelty_zh: 在冻结的STATE骨干上加入停止头与精炼token，并以层级退出深度作为模型条件化的稳定描述符。
llm.summary_zh: RefineRx在冻结的STATE骨干上训练oracle监督的停止头与精炼token，用学到的层级退出分布的期望深度描述扰动响应。在K562、HepG2、Jurkat与RPE1的重分析中，四个随机种子的平均两两Spearman相关为0.761至0.854；在两名CD4+ T细胞供体的输出中，跨供体一致性在静息与8小时为负，在48小时升至0.486。

title: An Ensemble Deep Learning Framework for Single-Cell Phenotypic Profiling of Escherichia coli under Antibiotic Stress
abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a pressing global health threat, requiring automated and adaptive methods to understand bacterial responses to antibiotics at the single-cell level. In this study, we present a deep learning and ensemble-based framework for morphological profiling and antibiotic classification of Escherichia coli using fluorescence microscopic images. Single-cell segmentation is performed with cellpose and auto-generated masks to ensure consistent feature extraction. Thirteen Deep learning architectures, including convolutional networks and vision transformers, are trained to classify untreated cells and those exposed to Chloramphenicol, Mecillinam, MP265, and Nalidixic acid. While the Swin Transformer achieves the highest individual accuracy at 91%, an ensemble combining Swin Transformer, CoaT, and ResNet18 further improves performance. The stacking ensemble provides improved results, with average precision, recall, and F1 scores of 94%. Beyond classification, the framework identifies distinct morphological profiles associated with each antibiotic, including characteristic alterations in cellular geometry, membrane structure, and nucleoid organization. By linking morphological phenotypes to antibiotic mechanisms, this approach establishes an imaging-based methodology for bacterial phenotyping, enables 1 faster antibiotic screening, and advances the study of antimicrobial resistance through quantitative microscopy.

title: Untreated controls reveal that pre-treatment prediction of cancer cell fate mostly reflects growth fitness
abstract: Background: Some cancer cells survive treatment without genetic change, and many studies suggest they can be recognised in advance from their gene expression. Sister-cell lineage tracing tests this. One daughter of a dividing cell is sequenced before treatment and the other treated. However, a cell whose sister survives may simply grow well. How much of the predictable signal reflects drug tolerance rather than growth fitness is unknown. Results: Using the identically processed untreated arm of the ReSisTrace experiment, we compared each drug-arm predictor with a fitness model trained on untreated cells. In 32,642 pre-treatment ovarian cancer cells, a linear model predicted the sister's fate with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.72–0.75, against 0.50–0.60 for published methods on olaparib; a graph neural network and two single-cell foundation models did no better. The fitness model, which never saw a drug, reached 0.70–0.73. The drug-specific gain was about 0.02 AUROC, positive in every arm, not reliably separable from zero, and at most about 0.05. The shared signal marked a proliferative, low-stress state that a label-free score largely recovered. In a second lineage system, pre-treatment clone size outpredicted expression under all six treatments, and in 11 patients the fitness state was depleted, not enriched, after chemotherapy. Conclusions: Most of what a pre-treatment transcriptome predicts about a cancer cell's fate is growth fitness rather than drug tolerance. Such claims should be tested against an untreated arm processed in the same way; our package persist.fitadj does this for any lineage-tracing design.

title: Prioritization of Androgenetic Alopecia-Associated Lactylation Sites through Multi-Omics Integration and the HybridKla Deep Learning Framework
abstract: Abstract The contribution of lysine lactylation to androgenetic alopecia (AGA) remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrated scalp single-cell transcriptomics, proteomics, lactylomics, and HybridKla-based deep learning to prioritize AGA-associated lactylation candidates. Single-cell data from three frontal–occipital donor pairs provided a T-cell-related transcriptional context, while proteomic and lactylomic profiling of two donor pairs identified 1,804 lactylation sites on 551 proteins. ZBTB7B, a transcription factor involved in T-cell lineage regulation, showed opposing regional trends in total-protein and modified-peptide abundance: frontal-to-occipital ratios were 1.806 for total ZBTB7B, 0.523 for K206-associated lactylated peptides, and 0.587 for K212-associated lactylated peptides. These directions were consistent across both donors, although neither site passed multiple-testing correction. To support candidate prioritization, we adapted HybridKla using 46,403 reference site records with protein-grouped five-fold partitioning for base-model evaluation. Five-score fusion yielded reported receiver operating characteristic and precision–recall areas under the curve of 0.8281 and 0.7984, respectively. Classification-head adaptation increased mean recall from 78.09% to 90.75% on 346 confirmed positive sites from 176 held-out proteins; this positive-only evaluation assessed detection sensitivity rather than overall classification performance. Both K206 and K212 were included among predicted-positive ZBTB7B sites and supported by mass-spectrometric localization records. Together, these findings prioritize ZBTB7B K206 and K212 as candidate sites for investigating lactylation-associated regulation in AGA. The integrated workflow connects tissue-level observations with residue-specific evidence, providing a focused basis for examining post-translational regulation within the follicular immune microenvironment.

title: Single‑Cell in silico Perturbation Uncovers a Ferroptosis Regulatory Network for Cigarette Smoke‑Induced Skin Aging and Identifies Dapivirine as a Candidate Agent.
abstract: Objective Cigarette smoke exposure induces cutaneous ferroptosis and accelerates skin aging, yet the core regulatory genes and targeted interventions remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key ferroptosis-driving genes underlying smoke-induced skin senescence, clarify their mechanisms, and screen candidate small molecules that reverse smoke-related skin damage. Methods Young and aged human skin single-cell transcriptomic data from the GEO database were processed for quality control, dimensional reduction, clustering, and cell-type annotation. The scTenifoldNet toolkit performed bidirectional in silico perturbation (virtual knockout and overexpression) of seven smoke-upregulated ferroptosis driver genes, with GO and KEGG enrichment on perturbation-derived DEGs. Based on the smoke-exposed skin dataset GSE148221, the DrugReflector deep-learning model conducted high-throughput virtual screening, followed by Cb-Dock2 molecular docking to verify binding affinity of the top compound to the seven ferroptosis proteins. Results Aging was the primary driver of global transcriptional remodeling, with aged skin showing prominent immune infiltration and elevated heterogeneity consistent with inflammaging. Bidirectional perturbation consistently identified KRT15 and CXCL14 as universal markers of disrupted ferroptosis signaling. Hub-gene dysregulation simultaneously triggered epidermal barrier dysfunction, cytoskeleton disorders, and chronic cutaneous inflammation. The anti-HIV agent dapivirine ranked first in AI screening and stably bound all seven targets, with particularly high affinity for CYBB, CHAC1, and HMOX1; no prior studies have reported its anti-skin-aging activity. Conclusion ABCC1, ATG4D, CHAC1, CYBB, HILPDA, HMOX1, and PGD constitute the core ferroptosis genes mediating smoke-induced skin aging. Repurposed dapivirine targets and suppresses the cutaneous ferroptosis pathway, showing promise against smoke-triggered skin senescence. These findings offer novel mechanistic insights into extrinsic skin aging and support anti-aging drug repurposing.

title: Single-Cell and Spatial Multi-Omics in Small-Intestinal Homeostasis and Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury: Current Advances, Applications, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: The intestinal tract acts as a dynamic barrier between the external and internal environments, and intestinal homeostasis fundamentally influences human health. This homeostasis depends on complex interactions among the epithelium, immune cells, and microbiota. Intestinal ischemia/reperfusion (II/R) disrupts these interactions and can cause local barrier failure and distant organ injury. However, the transition of the intestinal microenvironment from homeostasis to injury and repair remains incompletely characterized. This narrative review summarizes single-cell RNA sequencing, single-cell multi-omics, spatial transcriptomics, and spatial multi-omics, including their underlying methods. We compare intestinal reference atlases with direct II/R studies and examine how these approaches complement bulk sequencing and histology. Human intestinal atlases reveal spatially organized epithelial states, whereas experimental II/R studies identify altered Paneth-cell states, endothelial regenerative signals, and epithelial stress responses. These findings differ in their model systems, sampling times, and degree of functional validation. Dissociation bias, batch effects, limited biological replication, spatial resolution, and uncertain integration across modalities constrain interpretation. Most disease-specific evidence remains preclinical, and inferred cell interactions should not be equated with demonstrated therapeutic mechanisms. Translation will require standardized human sampling, spatial and protein-level validation, causal perturbation, and prospective assessment of clinically accessible markers. Single-cell and spatial omics can therefore refine mechanistic hypotheses and guide validation in II/R, but currently do not constitute established clinical diagnostic or treatment pathways.

title: Convergent Autoencoder and Machine Learning Methodologies for SARS-CoV-2 Essential Host Factor Identification based on Interferon Pathway Loss-of-Function Perturb-seq Data Mining
abstract: Introduction: The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the importance of understanding host-virus interactions, particularly the role of interferon (IFN) signaling pathways in viral pathogenesis. Methods: This study employed a comprehensive machine learning framework to analyze Perturb-seq data from SARS-CoV-2-infected Calu-3 respiratory epithelial cells to identify key host factors associated with viral infection under various IFN signaling conditions. We implemented two complementary feature selection strategies: Raw Feature Ranking using ten algorithms combined with IFS technology, and Autoencoder-based Feature Reconfiguration for dimensionality reduction, followed by ranking with the same algorithms combined with IFS. We compared expression differences between infected and uninfected cells in both IFN-knockout and control conditions to investigate distinct responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Results: In control conditions, Raw Feature Ranking identified important genes including FOS, JUN, B2M, PPIA, and MALAT1, known for their roles in viral pathogenesis, antigen processing, and inflammatory response. Under IFN knockout conditions, numerous mitochondrial genes (MT-ND3, MTCO1, MT-ND4L, MT-ND4, MT-CO3, MT-ATP6, MT-CO2, MT-CYB) emerged as key discriminatory features, suggesting mitochondrial dysfunction as a crucial mechanism when IFN signaling is compromised. Autoencoder-based methods showed close alignment with raw feature ranking, identifying 63 and 64 features in the IFN and Control groups, respectively, with 46 and 32 overlapping genes. Additional key factors included EEF1A1, KRT8, KRT19, MIF, SPINT2, and S100A10. Discussion: Enrichment analysis revealed consistent enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation and thermogenesis pathways across conditions, with IFN knockout cells specifically enriched for coronavirus disease pathways. Conclusion: This comprehensive approach provided robust biomarker identification and molecular insights into SARS-CoV-2 immune evasion mechanisms.

title: Uniformly processed single-cell CRISPRi screens: quality-controlled matrices and perturbation-effect estimates
abstract: Processed data underlying the manuscript "Transcriptional perturbation effects remain structured beyond the leading global trend". Twelve publicly available single-cell CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screens (Perturb-seq) were reprocessed with one pipeline (crispyx v0.1.4) and one set of quality-control settings: Replogle-GW-K562, Replogle-E-K562, Replogle-E-RPE1, Nadig-Jurkat, Nadig-HepG2, Huang-HCT116, Huang-HEK293T, Feng-GW-iPSC, Feng-TS-iPSC, Pan-GP-H1, VCC-H1, and Nourreddine-iPSC. Together, they cover more than 17 million cells. Feng-GW-iPSC is stored as two sub-screens (Feng-gwsf and Feng-gwsnf), and a subsampled version of VCC (VCC-subsampled) is also provided. Four types of files. Every archive is named by a type prefix followed by the dataset name (e.g. sc_Replogle-E-k562.zip), and the prefix is one of:"sc_" (single-cell data): the QC-filtered, log-normalized single-cell expression matrix (cells × genes) with per-cell metadata, including perturbation and batch labels. "effect_" (perturbation effects): per-perturbation effect estimates (perturbation × gene; perturbed minus matched control, batch-aware) with model-based and robust standard errors. "DE_" (differential expression): per-perturbation Wilcoxon rank-sum statistics (rank effect size, log fold change, z-score, p-value and Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted p-value), both pooled and batch-stratified (van Elteren). "split_" (split-half replicates): effect estimates recomputed on each half of five random 50:50 splits of the cells (seeds 0–4). For the three largest screens (Huang-HCT116, Huang-HEK293T and Nourreddine-GW-ipsc), these come as one archive per seed (e.g. split_Huang-HCT116_seed0.zip … split_Huang-HCT116_seed4.zip). VCC-subsampled has no split_ archive.Download only the file types and screens you need. QC: cells with fewer than 100 detected genes were removed; perturbations with fewer than 20 cells were removed; genes detected in fewer than 100 cells were removed; counts were normalized to 10^4 per cell and log1p-transformed. All matrices are AnnData .h5ad files (lossless gzip inside HDF5), grouped into store-mode .zip archives. README.md holds the full documentation and MANIFEST.csv, which lists every file with its size and MD5 checksum. Raw reads and original count matrices are not included; they are available from the original publications. If you use these data, please cite the accompanying manuscript and the original screen publications listed in the README.

llm.novelty_zh: 用同一套流程与质控阈值统一重处理12个公开CRISPRi筛选，并提供效应估计与拆分半重复数据。
llm.summary_zh: 对12个公开单细胞CRISPRi（Perturb-seq）筛选使用统一的crispyx流程与质控标准重新处理，覆盖超过1700万个细胞。数据包括QC后的表达矩阵、扰动效应估计、Wilcoxon差异表达统计以及五次随机50:50拆分的半细胞重复。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为扰动预测与可重复性评测提供了统一口径的大规模数据底座，便于跨数据集直接比较。
llm.limitations_zh: 仅包含CRISPRi筛选而非其他扰动形式，原始reads与原始计数矩阵未包含在内。

title: Unleashing AI for preclinical drug development
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping preclinical drug development across target discovery, therapeutic design, synthesis, functional characterization and safety assessment. In this review, we present an integrated view of AI across the preclinical pipeline, beginning with target identification, modality selection and representation learning for molecular, protein, structural, cellular and multimodal data. We then examine major generative modeling paradigms including autoregressive, latent-variable, diffusion, flow-based and guided approaches and their applications across small molecules, peptides, enzymes, antibodies, Tcell receptors and mRNA therapeutics. We discuss how these methods support de novo design, structure- and pocket-conditioned generation, sequence–structure co-design, affinity and activity optimization, developability engineering and synthesis-aware discovery. We further review AI-enabled retrosynthesis, reaction prediction and closed-loop experimental optimization, emphasizing the distinction between computational synthesizability and experimentally executable chemistry. Beyond molecular generation, we organize functional prediction from binding and kinetics through target engagement, pharmacological activity, mechanism of action, pathway response and phenotypic outcome. We also examine singlecell perturbation modeling, organoid-based drug-response prediction, toxicity and off-target assessment, and prospective validation across therapeutic modalities. Across these areas, we highlight the importance of uncertainty estimation, out-of-distribution generalization, reproducibility and experimentally grounded benchmarking. Finally, we discuss how integrating generative AI, mechanistic biology and iterative design–make–test–analyze cycles could transform AI from isolated predictive tools into decision-support systems for preclinical drug development.
affiliations: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

llm.novelty_zh: 综述 AI 在临床前药物开发各环节的应用，并强调不确定性估计与可重复基准的重要性。
llm.summary_zh: 该综述涵盖靶点识别、分子与蛋白生成、逆合成及功能与毒性预测，并讨论了单细胞扰动建模与类器官药物响应预测。作者强调不确定性估计、分布外泛化与实验基准的重要性。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为理解 AI 在临床前药物开发中的整体图景提供了参考，可用于定位相关的分子生成与扰动建模研究。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要为综述性文章，未提及文献纳入标准与定量评价。

title: Identification and validation of biomarkers related to oxidative stress in pediatric sepsis utilizing WGCNA and multiple machine learning algorithms.
abstract: Background This research aimed to identify novel oxidative stress (OS)-related biomarkers and develop predictive models for the early detection of pediatric sepsis. Methods Five open-access datasets from the gene expression omnibus database were analyzed, which included peripheral whole blood samples from children with sepsis and healthy controls. Using bioinformatics approaches, we identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs) associated with OS. We then combined weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and multiple machine learning algorithms (ML) to identify seven candidate genes, constructed a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network to screen six hub genes, and evaluated their correlations with the immune microenvironment. We subsequently evaluated the diagnostic performance of the hub genes using training datasets (GSE26440 and GSE26378) and validation datasets (GSE13904, GSE8121, and GSE9692). Moreover, molecular docking analysis revealed interactions between hub gene-encoded proteins and small-molecule compounds, which helps predict drug sensitivity. Results The study identified 36 differentially expressed oxidative stress-related genes (OSRGs). Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses highlighted these genes' roles in regulating inflammatory responses and reactive oxygen species metabolism. Seven candidate genes were identified using machine learning algorithms. Subsequently, through protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, six hub genes, namely, GADD45A, HP, MAPK14, PGD, RETN, and S100A9, were identified as having significant diagnostic potential. Immune cell deconvolution analysis of peripheral blood transcriptomes suggested that hub genes related to oxidative stress may be linked to alterations in the composition of peripheral blood immune cells. The diagnostic performance of the six hub genes was validated with area under the curve (AUC) values between 0.908 and 0.982, showing their promising diagnostic performance. Additionally, molecular docking analysis suggested that small molecules Doxycycline, Ralimetinib mesylate, Tasquinimod might interact with the identified hub genes, which opens up new treatment options. Conclusion Our research not only reveals potential diagnostic biomarkers of pediatric sepsis but also sets the stage for future studies. These studies aim to translate our findings into clinical practice, enabling earlier and more accurate diagnoses as well as targeted therapies to improve outcomes for children.
affiliations: Department of Pediatrics, Liaoning Maternal and Child Health Hospital, Shenyang, Liaoning, China.

llm.novelty_zh: 将氧化应激相关差异基因与WGCNA及多种机器学习结合，筛选脓毒症诊断标志物。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究联合五个GEO公共数据集，通过差异表达、WGCNA与多种机器学习方法筛选氧化应激相关的六个枢纽基因。作者报告其在验证集上AUC为0.908至0.982，并用分子对接探讨三种小分子的潜在相互作用。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为儿童脓毒症的早期识别提供候选生物标志物线索。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: Topology-adjusted knockout (TAKO): interpretable <i>in silico</i> single-gene knockout ranking on wild-type single-cell gene regulatory networks.
abstract: Predicting single-gene knockout effects from wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data remains challenging when perturbation experiments are costly and existing approaches require knockout-specific model training. Here we introduce Topology-Adjusted Knockout (TAKO), a computationally efficient WT-only framework for single-gene KO impact ranking on single-cell gene regulatory networks. The method applies a strict cut-in-and-out intervention on network transition dynamics and quantifies impact by contrasting stationary propagation profiles before and after perturbation under the same restart distribution. In SERGIO simulations, TAKO recovered direct regulator-target structure but did not show a consistent global advantage over a matched absolute Pearson-correlation ranking across network sizes. Direct evaluation against measured responses in Trem2 and Nkx2-1 KO data likewise yielded mixed global discrimination, although TAKO contained more differentially expressed genes among the top-ranked candidates in both examples. These results position TAKO as a fast, interpretable topology-based prioritisation method rather than a generally superior predictor of post-KO expression responses.
affiliations: Graduate School of Interdisciplinary Information Studies, The University of Tokyo, Tokyo, Japan.
Interfaculty Initiative in Information Studies, The University of Tokyo, Tokyo, Japan.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出仅依赖野生型单细胞基因调控网络的单基因敲除排序方法TAKO，通过稳态传播谱的前后对比计算影响。
llm.summary_zh: TAKO在野生型单细胞基因调控网络上施加切入切出式干预，比较干预前后的稳态传播谱以排序单基因敲除的影响，无需针对敲除训练。SERGIO模拟中其未稳定优于绝对Pearson相关排序，在Trem2与Nkx2-1敲除数据中的结果也喜忧参半。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为低成本的无扰动数据敲除效应预测提供了可解释的思路，并如实报告了其局限。
llm.limitations_zh: 在模拟与真实敲除数据上均未表现出稳定的全局优势。

title: Recognizing senescent vascular smooth muscle cells in diabetic atherosclerosis: biomarkers, transcriptomic signatures, and methodological validity.
abstract: Diabetic atherosclerosis represents the most severe macrovascular complication of diabetes mellitus and a major contributor to global morbidity and mortality. Senescence of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) has been increasingly recognized as a central mechanism driving plaque formation, progression, and instability under diabetic conditions. Yet identifying senescent VSMCs reliably remains difficult: available biomarkers lack specificity, transcriptomic signatures vary considerably across studies, and no consensus has emerged on how senescence should be verified methodologically. This review consolidates current knowledge on senescent VSMC identification in diabetic atherosclerosis. We begin with the pathobiological routes through which hyperglycemia drives VSMC senescence, including oxidative stress, DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and metabolic reprogramming. We then present a multidimensional classification of senescence-associated biomarkers, spanning cell cycle regulators, senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal), telomere-related markers, the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), calcification markers, and emerging non-coding RNA signatures, and assess the applicability and shortcomings of each. Transcriptomic signatures derived from single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and flow cytometry are then integrated to map the heterogeneity of senescent VSMC subpopulations and their functional roles within atherosclerotic plaques. We next appraise the methodological validity of existing detection strategies, comparing in vitro high-glucose models, in vivo diabetic animal models, and clinical specimens, and trace the sources of inter-study inconsistency, including spatial heterogeneity, cross-sectional designs, and the absence of standardized protocols. Finally, we outline a stepwise identification pipeline extending from molecular markers to functional validation and multi-omics integration, and consider future prospects such as senolytic therapies and targeted delivery systems. By providing this methodological reference, we hope to support both basic research and clinical translation and to push the field toward more precise, standardized identification of senescent VSMCs.
affiliations: The First Affiliated Hospital, College of Clinical Medicine, Henan University of Science and Technology, Luoyang, China.
Luoyang Key Laboratory of Cardiovascular Science, The First Affiliated Hospital, Henan University of Science and Technology, Luoyang, China.

llm.novelty_zh: 综述性质，提出糖尿病动脉粥样硬化中衰老VSMC的分步识别流程，无新实验。
llm.summary_zh: 该综述讨论了高糖驱动VSMC衰老的机制，并对细胞周期、SA-β-gal、端粒、SASP和非编码RNA等生物标志物进行分类评估。文章还比较了体外、动物和临床样本的检测方法学差异。

title: AI and computational methods for reconstructing cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptome and chromatin accessibility data in cancer: methods, applications, and perspectives.
abstract: Tumor heterogeneity is shaped by genetic, epigenetic, microenvironmental, and stochastic factors, among which cell-state-specific regulatory programs are a major determinant. Gene regulatory networks provide a systems-level model linking transcription factors, cis-regulatory elements, and target genes. Paired single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) measure chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cell, offering a direct view of regulatory elements and transcriptional output; matched-but-unpaired, imputed, and single-modality designs can extend coverage but introduce additional assumptions and artifacts. This mini-review focuses on AI and computational methods for reconstructing cell-state-specific GRNs from single-cell transcriptome and chromatin accessibility data in cancer. We define inclusion criteria, distinguish same-cell paired, matched-unpaired, imputed, and single-modality designs, and organize methods by inference objective and input requirement. We cover motif/co-accessibility inference, deep integration and graph learning, dynamic and cell-state-specific modeling, and virtual perturbation. We then discuss applications in epithelial-mesenchymal transition, treatment resistance, lineage plasticity, and tumor subtyping, emphasizing an evidence hierarchy from statistical association to directional prediction, in silico perturbation, and experimentally supported causal regulation. Finally, we examine benchmarking, limitations, and translational prospects. These approaches may help convert GRNs from descriptive maps into testable models of tumor regulation, but clinical utility still requires prospective validation.
affiliations: Department of Internal Medicine, Shaoxing Second Hospital Medical Community General Hospital, Shaoxing, Zhejiang, China.

llm.novelty_zh: 综述癌症中基于单细胞转录组与染色质可及性重建细胞状态特异性 GRN 的 AI 方法，并按证据层级组织。
llm.summary_zh: 这篇小型综述依据配对、非配对、插补和单模态等数据设计，对重建细胞状态特异性 GRN 的计算方法进行分类，涵盖模体与共可及性推断、深度整合、动态建模以及虚拟扰动。作者按从统计关联到实验支持的因果调控证据层级，讨论其在上皮间质转化和耐药等场景中的应用。

title: From density to spatial function: spatial multi-omics, composite biomarker design, and therapeutic engineering of tertiary lymphoid structures in solid tumors.
abstract: Background Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) have emerged as clinically relevant immune niches associated with improved survival and enhanced response to immune checkpoint inhibitors across multiple solid tumors. However, translational evaluation remains dominated by density-based scoring, which inadequately captures the functional heterogeneity of histologically similar lymphoid aggregates. This review synthesizes recent advances in spatial biology that support a shift from counting TLSs to interpreting them as spatially organized immune microenvironmental units embedded within local tumor ecosystems. Main body Evidence from spatial transcriptomics, multiplexed imaging, single-cell profiling, computational pathology, and spatial-proteomic approaches converges on four coupled requirements for productive TLS function: stromal licensing through lymphotoxin-dependent chemokine circuits, vascular competence mediated by specialized high endothelial venules, helper T-cell programs that bridge follicular and cytotoxic immunity, and a permissive metabolic context that enables maturation. Spatial studies further show that regulatory infiltration, suppressive plasma-cell programs, and metabolic disruption can decouple structural presence from effective antitumor immunity. Across tumor types, these insights indicate that biomarker performance improves when TLS density is integrated with maturity, anatomical location, HEV coupling, immune composition, and treatment context rather than used as a standalone metric. We further discuss how spatial analyses reveal actionable pathways for inducing or reprogramming TLSs and outline a staged, module-matched composite biomarker workflow combining digital pathology, targeted multiplexed imaging, and focused molecular or metabolic augmentation. Conclusions TLSs should be regarded as spatially organized, functionally heterogeneous immune microenvironmental units rather than biologically equivalent lymphoid aggregates. A spatial-functional framework helps explain productive, arrested, and suppressive TLS states, provides a basis for next-generation composite biomarkers, and supports module-matched therapeutic strategies tailored to the stromal, vascular, helper-cell, or metabolic bottleneck limiting TLS function in individual tumors. The immediate next step is prospective validation of a minimal TLS panel across defined treatment contexts.
affiliations: The Sixth Clinical Medical College of Guangzhou Medical University (Qingyuan People's Hospital), Qingyuan, China.
Department of Oncology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Shenzhen University, The Second People's Hospital of Shenzhen, Shenzhen, China.

llm.novelty_zh: 综述性质，主张以空间功能框架替代TLS密度计数，并构建复合生物标志物流程。

llm.limitations_zh: 摘要提及：需要在明确治疗背景下对最小TLS面板进行前瞻性验证。

title: Autonomous AI research agents in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma immunology: from multimodal evidence to experimental validation.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most challenging malignancies due to profound biological heterogeneity, complex stromal organization, and limited responsiveness to current immunotherapies. Recent advances in single-cell sequencing, spatial omics, digital pathology, and multimodal profiling have revealed that PDAC immune states are shaped not only by cellular composition but also by spatial organization, treatment context, and patient-specific evolutionary trajectories. However, the increasing complexity and fragmentation of biomedical evidence create substantial challenges for conventional artificial intelligence (AI) approaches that are typically optimized for predefined analytical tasks. Autonomous AI research agents represent an emerging paradigm that extends beyond predictive modeling by integrating scientific reasoning, retrieval of heterogeneous biomedical knowledge, computational tool orchestration, workflow adaptation, and evidence traceability. In this Review, we examine how agentic AI systems may contribute to PDAC immunology research, from characterization of immune ecosystems and spatial cellular interactions to biomarker discovery, neoantigen prioritization, and experimental protocol design. We distinguish AI agents from conventional task-specific models and discuss essential capabilities required for reliable biomedical research, including planning, tool use, verification, memory, provenance tracking, and human oversight. Despite promising technical demonstrations in biomedical domains, direct evidence supporting fully autonomous AI-driven discovery and validation in PDAC remains limited. Therefore, we propose a disease-oriented evaluation framework emphasizing benchmark task design, appropriate human and computational comparators, reproducibility assessment, and experimental validation. Future PDAC-specific AI research agents should prioritize evidence-aware reasoning, multimodal integration, calibrated uncertainty, and transparent computational-experimental workflows. Such systems may ultimately accelerate mechanistic discovery and precision immunology, while maintaining rigorous standards for biological validity, reproducibility, and responsible scientific practice.
affiliations: General Surgery Center, First Hospital of Jilin University, Changchun, Jilin, China.
School of Nursing, Jilin University, Changchun, China.
Department of Ophthalmology, First Hospital of Jilin University, Changchun, Jilin, China.

llm.novelty_zh: 综述，提出面向胰腺导管腺癌免疫学的自主 AI 研究代理评估框架。
llm.summary_zh: 该综述讨论自主 AI 研究代理在胰腺导管腺癌免疫学中的应用潜力，包括免疫生态、空间细胞互作、生物标志物与新抗原筛选以及实验方案设计。作者区分了代理与传统任务模型，列举规划、工具调用、验证、记忆与溯源等能力，并提出以基准任务和实验验证为核心的评估框架。

title: Decoding molecular heterogeneity in lupus nephritis: integrating single-cell and spatial multi-omics for endotype-driven precision therapeutics.
abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) develops in 40-60% of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and remains the leading cause of renal morbidity and progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD). While the upstream immunological events initiating LN-including loss of self-tolerance, pathogenic autoantibody production, glomerular immune complex deposition, and type I interferon (IFN) activation-are broadly shared, accumulating evidence demonstrates that these convergent triggers give rise to molecularly heterogeneous tissue injury programs at the renal level. This fundamental divergence provides a mechanistic explanation for the inconsistent therapeutic responses observed with standardized immunosuppressive protocols. Advances in single-cell transcriptomics, spatial gene expression mapping, CITE-seq, and cross-platform multi-omic integration have deconvolved this heterogeneity into at least five recognizable tissue-level injury programs: (i) an IFN-γ-polarized macrophage-tubular epithelial cell co-activation circuit, (ii) a Tfh-B cell ectopic germinal center pathway, (iii) a neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-driven inflammatory cascade, (iv) a podocyte-autonomous injury program, and (v) a TREM2+ macrophage-orchestrated fibrotic program. Concurrently, multiplexed urinary biomarker platforms are under development as non-invasive surrogates for tissue-level pathogenic activity. This review synthesizes current understanding of disease mechanisms, molecular profiling evidence, biomarker candidates, and mechanism-directed therapies corresponding to each tissue injury program. We map existing and investigational agents-including anifrolumab, obinutuzumab, voclosporin, CAR-T cell therapy, and complement inhibitors-to their mechanistic targets and delineate the design requirements for prospective biomarker-stratified trials essential to validating molecularly guided treatment selection.
affiliations: Department of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Jiangxi University of Chinese Medicine, Nanchang, Jiangxi, China.
Department of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Gaoxin Branch of the First Affiliated Hospital, Nanchang University, Nanchang, Jiangxi, China.

llm.summary_zh: 该综述整合单细胞与空间多组学证据，将狼疮性肾炎的组织损伤归纳为 IFN-γ 相关巨噬细胞-肾小管上皮细胞共激活、Tfh-B 生发中心、NET 驱动炎症、足细胞自主损伤与 TREM2 巨噬细胞纤维化五类程序。文章还梳理了相应的靶向药物与尿液生物标志物候选。
